Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the Solvency II economic balance sheet (S.02.01.02) and SFCR Section D 'Valuation for Solvency Purposes' for every solo undertaking and the group; escalates valuation judgement to the Chief Financial Officer

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Art. 296(2)-(4) re-read on EUR-Lex in its consolidated form as at the 31 December reference date, together with Directive 2009/138/EC Art. 51 and Art. 75 and the EIOPA Guidelines on recognition and valuation of assets and liabilities other than technical provisions; group articles 359-371 checked for the group SFCR

In-scope processes.value: Year-end hard close → Art. 75 valuation of assets, technical provisions and other liabilities → IFRS-to-Solvency II difference bridge → drafting of SFCR Sections D.1 to D.4 for each EEA solo entity and the consolidated group

In-scope systems.value: IFRS ledger balances consolidated in the close tool, revalued through the Solvency II adjustment layer; technical provisions imported from the actuarial platform; the bridge and Section D drafts held against the same close period

Compliance procedure documented.value: Solvency II Valuation and SFCR Section D Procedure — Art. 75 valuation hierarchy (quoted market prices, quoted prices for similar assets, alternative valuation methods), the per-line IFRS-to-SII bridge template, the technical-provisions bases/methods/assumptions disclosure set, and the quantitative plus qualitative explanation table required by Art. 296(1)-(3)

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Financial Officer and noted by the Audit Committee; re-approved each year before the hard close and re-opened on any amending Delegated Regulation or revised EIOPA valuation Guideline

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Solo SFCR disclosed within 14 weeks of the 31 December year-end and the group SFCR within 20 weeks; Section D must be draft-complete at year-end plus 8 weeks so the external auditor has four clear weeks on the relevant elements

Deadline reminders configured.value: Close-calendar tasks fire at year-end plus 4, 8 and 11 weeks against every Section D subsection owner, with a daily countdown on the group SFCR from week 16

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Valuation files per balance-sheet line, pricing-source captures, the signed IFRS-to-SII bridge, actuarial function TP sign-off and the published SFCR PDF retained 10 years from disclosure in the financial reporting repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any balance-sheet line whose IFRS-to-SII difference exceeds the disclosure materiality floor without a quantified and worded explanation is logged as a disclosure exception with root cause, owner and a correction date before disclosure

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The CFO signs every valuation-method change, every alternative valuation method under Art. 10(5)-(7) of the Delegated Regulation, and every post-disclosure SFCR correction

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every populated line of S.02.01.02 at 31 December for each solo entity and the group, plus every numeric assertion and every bases/methods/assumptions paragraph in SFCR Sections D.1 to D.4

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Every line whose IFRS-to-SII difference exceeds 2 percent of eligible own funds or EUR 5 million must carry both a quantified difference and a worded driver; an unexplained line, an unsourced valuation input, or a Section D figure that disagrees with S.02.01.02 is a fail and blocks disclosure

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is annual, so the full test runs on the 31 December balance sheet during the hard close, with an abbreviated dry run on the 30 June figures to prove the bridge and the Section D template before year-end

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must be outside the statutory reporting line and must not have prepared or reviewed any sampled valuation file or Section D paragraph

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual SFCR Section D test workpaper — population extract of S.02.01.02, sample selection with seed, re-performance notes, bridge recomputation and exception log — filed in the financial reporting repository under the reporting year

Regulator-ready documentation.value: A per-line valuation dossier (input source, valuation technique, Art. 75 hierarchy level, IFRS carrying amount, SII value, difference and driver) deliverable to the national competent authority within 10 working days of a Section D query

Regulator response path.value: The Statutory Reporting Manager drafts NCA responses on Section D; the Chief Financial Officer clears any answer that concedes a valuation error, and any restatement of a disclosed SFCR goes to the Audit Committee before it is re-published

checklist.step: Lock the year-end ledger and open the Solvency II valuation file
actions: In the close tool open the 31 December period for each reporting entity and confirm the Controller has set the ledger status to Closed so no further IFRS postings can land.
Export the closing trial balance by account and entity to the Solvency II valuation workbook, keeping the IFRS carrying amount as the untouched left-hand column.

Map every trial-balance account to its S.02.01.02 line (R0030 intangibles, R0040 deferred tax assets, R0070 property, R0080-R0210 investments, R0270-R0300 receivables, R0510-R0690 liabilities) using the standing account-to-template map.
List any account with no mapping and clear it with the Controller before valuation starts; an unmapped account cannot appear in the balance sheet.
Save the file as SII-valuation-<entity>-<year>.xlsx in the year-end folder of the financial reporting repository.
checklist.done: the closed IFRS trial balance is loaded, every account maps to an S.02.01.02 line, and no unmapped balances remain.

checklist.step: Value the asset side under the Article 75 hierarchy and record the source of every price
actions: Extract the 31 December holdings file from the investment book of record with market value, dirty price, accrued interest, CIC code and pricing source per security.
Classify each holding into the Art. 75 / Delegated Regulation Art. 10 hierarchy: quoted market prices in active markets, quoted prices for similar assets, or alternative valuation method.
For alternative-valuation holdings (unlisted equity, private debt, property, unquoted funds) attach the model, key inputs and the date of the last independent valuation.
Reverse the IFRS amortised-cost carrying amounts for held-to-collect debt and replace them with fair value, recording the difference per security.
Hand the priced file to the Statutory Reporting Manager with a signed statement of the pricing sources used and any stale-price overrides.
checklist.done: every asset line carries a Solvency II fair value, an Art. 75 hierarchy level and a named pricing source, with alternative-valuation holdings supported by a dated model.

checklist.step: Revalue participations and related undertakings on the adjusted equity method
actions: List every participation and related undertaking from the group structure chart with its percentage holding and whether it is quoted.

Apply the Delegated Regulation Art. 13 order: quoted market price where an active market exists, otherwise the adjusted equity method using the related undertaking's own Solvency II excess of assets over liabilities.

For non-insurance related undertakings where the adjusted equity method is impracticable, apply IFRS equity method with goodwill and intangibles stripped to nil and document why the higher method was not available.
Post the resulting values to S.02.01.02 R0090-R0100 and record the difference from the IFRS carrying amount on the bridge.
Ask the Corporate Secretary to confirm no participation was acquired or disposed after the reference date without disclosure.
checklist.done: each participation is valued at the highest available point of the Art. 13 hierarchy with the method and its justification recorded.

checklist.step: Import technical provisions and the risk margin from the actuarial platform
actions: Run the signed-off year-end valuation model and export best estimate and risk margin split by line of business and by homogeneous risk group.
Confirm the discount curve used is the EIOPA risk-free term structure published for 31 December, including the volatility adjustment and any matching adjustment portfolio approval reference.
Reconcile the exported best estimate to the reserving committee paper, agreeing the figure to the euro before it enters the balance sheet.
Post best estimate and risk margin to S.02.01.02 R0510-R0690 by segment and record the transitional measure on technical provisions separately if applied.
Write the bases, methods and main assumptions memo covering contract boundaries, expense assumptions, lapse and mortality bases, and the risk-margin cost-of-capital rate of 6 percent.
checklist.done: technical provisions in the balance sheet tie exactly to the signed actuarial run and a bases/methods/assumptions memo exists per segment.

checklist.step: Value other liabilities including pensions, provisions and subordinated debt
actions: Pull the IAS 19 defined-benefit obligation and plan asset schedule from the Group actuary and carry the net position across unchanged, since IAS 19 measurement is accepted for Solvency II.

Fair value subordinated liabilities and financial liabilities without adjusting for the change in own credit standing after initial recognition, and record the own-credit adjustment reversal on the bridge.

Re-measure provisions and contingent liabilities: recognise contingent liabilities that are material under Delegated Regulation Art. 14 at the expected present value of future cash flows, which IFRS leaves off balance sheet.
Strip goodwill to nil and value intangibles at nil unless they can be sold separately and a quoted price for similar assets exists.
Send the completed other-liabilities schedule to the Statutory Reporting Manager with a line-by-line note of each departure from IFRS.
checklist.done: other liabilities are stated on a Solvency II basis with goodwill and non-saleable intangibles at nil and every departure from IFRS noted.

checklist.step: Recompute deferred tax on the Solvency II temporary differences
actions: Take the completed Solvency II asset and liability values and compare each to its tax base in the local tax computation.
Compute the deferred tax position on the resulting temporary differences at the enacted rate per jurisdiction, then post it to R0040 (DTA) or R0780 (DTL).
Test recoverability of any net deferred tax asset against forecast taxable profit and the loss-carry-forward rules of the jurisdiction, and document the evidence relied on.
Split the deferred tax adjustment on the bridge between the IFRS deferred tax already booked and the incremental Solvency II amount.
Have the Tax Director sign the recoverability assessment before the figure is used in own funds.
checklist.done: deferred tax is recomputed on the Solvency II bases, split on the bridge, and any net DTA carries a signed recoverability assessment.

checklist.step: Build the IFRS-to-Solvency II difference bridge line by line
actions: Lay out one bridge row per S.02.01.02 line: IFRS carrying amount, each valuation adjustment as its own column, Solvency II value, absolute difference and difference as a percentage of eligible own funds.

Attribute every adjustment to a named driver - fair valuing of amortised-cost debt, goodwill and intangibles written to nil, contract-boundary difference in technical provisions, risk margin added, contingent liabilities recognised, own-credit reversal, deferred tax on the above.
Foot the bridge so total assets less total liabilities equals the excess of assets over liabilities carried into S.23.01 own funds; investigate any residual before proceeding.
Flag every line breaching the disclosure materiality floor of 2 percent of eligible own funds or EUR 5 million as requiring both a number and a sentence in Section D.
Circulate the bridge to the Controller and the Valuation Actuary for line-owner confirmation.
checklist.done: the bridge foots to the excess of assets over liabilities, every adjustment has a named driver, and material lines are flagged for narrative.

checklist.step: Draft SFCR Section D.1 on the valuation of assets
actions: Write one subsection per material asset class stating the value, the valuation basis, the method and the main assumptions, as required by Delegated Regulation Art. 296(1)(a).
For each class add the quantitative difference from the financial statements taken straight from the bridge, plus a qualitative explanation of what drives it.
Describe the alternative valuation methods used, the assets they were applied to, and how the assumptions on which they rely are validated - Art. 10(5)-(7) requires this.
State explicitly that no changes were made to the recognition and valuation bases during the period, or describe each change and quantify its effect.
Hand the draft to the Controller for agreement that every figure quoted matches the audited financial statements.
checklist.done: Section D.1 covers every material asset class with value, basis, method, assumptions and a quantified plus worded difference from the financial statements.

checklist.step: Draft Section D.2 on technical provisions with the actuarial function
actions: State, by line of business, the value of technical provisions split into best estimate and risk margin, with the bases, methods and main assumptions behind each.
Describe the level of uncertainty in the amount of technical provisions and the drivers of movement since the prior year-end.

Disclose use of the matching adjustment, the volatility adjustment, the transitional risk-free rate and the transitional deduction to technical provisions, with the quantified impact of setting each to zero, as Art. 296(2)(d) requires.

Explain the material differences between the Solvency II technical provisions and the technical provisions in the financial statements - contract boundaries, discounting, prudence margins, risk margin.
Sign the section on behalf of the actuarial function and file the sign-off with the reserving committee minutes.
checklist.done: Section D.2 gives best estimate and risk margin by line of business, the LTG measure impacts, and a signed actuarial function attestation.

checklist.step: Draft Sections D.3 and D.4 on other liabilities and alternative methods
actions: Write Section D.3 with the value, basis, method and main assumptions for each material other-liability class - pensions, provisions, subordinated liabilities, deferred tax, payables.
Quantify and explain each material difference from the financial statement carrying amount, referencing the bridge row.
In Section D.4 describe any other material information on valuation, including leases, financial guarantees, and any judgement calls that could reasonably have gone the other way.
State the recognition of contingent liabilities that are not recognised under IFRS and how their expected present value was derived.
Route both sections to the Statutory Reporting Manager for consolidation into the SFCR master document.
checklist.done: Sections D.3 and D.4 are drafted with a quantified and worded difference for every material other-liability class.

checklist.step: Tie every Section D figure back to the quantitative reporting templates
actions: Build a tie-out schedule listing every number printed in Sections D.1 to D.4 next to its source cell reference in S.02.01.02, S.12.01, S.17.01 or S.22.01.
Investigate and clear any difference, including rounding presentation - the SFCR narrative is disclosed in thousands while the templates report in units.
Confirm the group SFCR figures reconcile to the sum of the solo entities plus consolidation adjustments, and that intra-group eliminations are disclosed.
Attach the tie-out schedule to the SFCR working file so a reviewer can trace any narrative figure in one step.
checklist.done: every narrative figure in Section D traces to a named template cell and the tie-out schedule shows no unexplained difference.

checklist.step: Run the Article 296 disclosure completeness check
actions: Open the consolidated text of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Art. 296 and list each required disclosure element as its own checklist row.
Walk the draft SFCR and record for each row the section and paragraph that satisfies it, or mark it Not Addressed.
Repeat the walk against Directive 2009/138/EC Art. 51 for the wider SFCR structure and Arts. 359-371 for the group SFCR content.
Return every Not Addressed row to its section owner with a two-day fix window and re-walk once fixed.
File the completed completeness matrix as the evidence that Art. 296 was addressed element by element.
checklist.done: the Art. 296 completeness matrix shows a section and paragraph reference against every required element with no Not Addressed rows.

checklist.step: Obtain external audit clearance on the relevant elements
actions: Deliver the balance sheet, own funds template and Section D draft to the external auditor at year-end plus 8 weeks per the agreed timetable.
Work the auditor's requests on valuation inputs, alternative valuation models and the technical provisions specialist review.
Log every proposed audit adjustment on the bridge, post the accepted ones and record the reasoning for any that management declines.
Obtain the auditor's clearance on the relevant elements of the SFCR before the document goes to the Board.
checklist.done: the external auditor has cleared the relevant elements and all accepted adjustments are posted to the balance sheet and the bridge.

checklist.step: Secure administrative body approval of the SFCR before disclosure
actions: Load the final SFCR, the bridge, the Art. 296 completeness matrix and the auditor clearance into the board portal at least 10 working days before the approval meeting.
Table the approval resolution: the administrative, management or supervisory body approves the SFCR and confirms it is prepared in accordance with the Directive and the Delegated Regulation.
Record director questions and management answers in the minutes, particularly on valuation judgement and the LTG measure impacts.
Capture the signed resolution and the approval date, which is the point from which the 14-week solo and 20-week group clocks are measured as met.
checklist.done: a signed board resolution approving the SFCR exists and is dated before the disclosure deadline.

checklist.step: Publish the SFCR and archive the valuation evidence
actions: Publish the approved SFCR on the undertaking's website in a permanently accessible location and record the publication URL and timestamp.
Send the SFCR and the annexed templates to the national competent authority through the supervisory reporting channel and keep the acknowledgement.
Move the valuation workbooks, pricing captures, actuarial sign-off, bridge, tie-out schedule and completeness matrix into the financial reporting repository under the reporting year.
Apply the 10-year retention label and confirm the index makes the record searchable by entity, reporting year and balance-sheet line.
checklist.done: the SFCR is published and acknowledged, and the full valuation evidence set is archived under a 10-year retention label.

testing.step: Build the population of balance-sheet lines and Section D assertions
actions: Extract every populated cell of S.02.01.02 at 31 December for each solo entity and the group into the test workpaper.
Add one population row for each numeric assertion and each bases/methods/assumptions paragraph in Sections D.1 to D.4.
Reconcile the extracted line count to the Art. 296 completeness matrix so no disclosure element is missing from the population.
Record the extraction date, the source file version and the extractor, and sign the population as complete.
testing.done: the population covers every populated balance-sheet line and every Section D assertion, reconciled to the completeness matrix and signed.

testing.step: Reconcile the Solvency II balance sheet to the audited financial statements
actions: Agree the IFRS column of the bridge to the audited primary statements line by line, not in total.
Foot the bridge and confirm total assets less total liabilities equals the excess of assets over liabilities carried into S.23.01.01 R0700.
Confirm the trial balance used was the closed period version and that no post-close IFRS journal landed after the extract.
Treat any residual that management describes as a rounding plug as an exception and quantify it.
testing.done: the bridge agrees to the audited statements line by line and foots to the excess of assets over liabilities with no plug.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of balance-sheet lines and narrative paragraphs
actions: Take 100 percent of lines whose Solvency II value exceeds 5 percent of total assets and 100 percent of lines valued by an alternative valuation method.
Take 20 further lines by seeded random selection from the remainder, plus 10 Section D paragraphs, for a minimum of 40 sample rows.
Record the seed, the population size, the stratification rule and the selection date so the sample can be re-drawn independently.
Confirm the sample includes at least one line from each of assets, technical provisions and other liabilities.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible from a recorded seed and covers all alternative-valuation lines and all three balance-sheet blocks.

testing.step: Re-perform the asset valuations in the investment book of record
actions: For each sampled asset line, pull the 31 December holdings and prices from the investment system independently of the reporting file.
Re-price a minimum of 15 securities against an external source and compare to the value used, before looking at the valuation workbook.
Check the Art. 75 hierarchy level assigned is defensible - a quoted price available in an active market cannot be overridden by a model.
Screenshot the pricing source screen for each re-performed security into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled asset line has an independent re-priced value, an assessed hierarchy level and a captured pricing source.

testing.step: Trace technical provisions to the signed actuarial run
actions: Open the model run referenced in the reserving committee paper and confirm the run identifier matches the one cited in the SFCR working file.
Agree best estimate and risk margin by line of business from the run output to S.02.01.02 R0510-R0690 and to S.12.01 / S.17.01.
Confirm the EIOPA risk-free curve version used is the one published for 31 December and that the volatility adjustment applied matches the approved portfolio.
Recompute the risk margin at the 6 percent cost-of-capital rate on the projected SCR run-off and compare to the reported figure.
testing.done: technical provisions trace to a named model run, the correct published curve, and a recomputed risk margin within tolerance.

testing.step: Recompute the materiality threshold and test explanation completeness
actions: Recompute the disclosure floor as 2 percent of eligible own funds and compare it to EUR 5 million, taking the lower as the operative threshold.
Apply the recomputed threshold to every bridge row, not just the rows management flagged, and list any line that should have been flagged and was not.
For each flagged line confirm Section D carries both the quantified difference and a worded driver - a number with no sentence is a fail, as is a sentence with no number.
Record each unexplained or partially explained line as an exception with the amount involved.
testing.done: the threshold is independently recomputed and every line above it carries both a quantified and a qualitative explanation, or is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Trace Section D narrative assertions to underlying evidence
actions: For each sampled narrative paragraph, request the source document that supports the assertion - valuation model, actuarial memo, tax recoverability paper, board minute.
Confirm the assertion is supported as written, including claims that no valuation basis changed during the period.
Check the alternative valuation method descriptions name the assets, the method, the key assumptions and the validation performed.
Log any assertion that is unsupported, overstated or contradicted by the evidence.
testing.done: every sampled narrative assertion traces to a dated source document that supports it as written.

testing.step: Cross-check the SFCR narrative against the reported templates
actions: Take 25 figures printed in Sections D.1 to D.4 and agree each to the cell in the submitted S.02.01, S.12.01, S.17.01, S.22.01 or S.23.01 instance.
Confirm the units and scaling stated in the narrative match the template basis and that no figure was restated between narrative and template.
For the group SFCR, agree the consolidated figures to the sum of solo submissions plus disclosed consolidation adjustments.
Log any narrative-to-template disagreement as an exception regardless of size.
testing.done: all cross-checked narrative figures agree to the submitted template cells with units and scaling consistent.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and correction date
actions: Raise one GRC issue per exception carrying the entity, the S.02.01.02 line, the Section D paragraph and the amount involved.
Assign a root cause from the standard set - unmapped account, stale price, wrong hierarchy level, missing bridge driver, narrative not updated from prior year, tie-out not performed.
Set an owner and a correction date that lands before the disclosure deadline; exceptions found after disclosure trigger a restatement assessment with the CFO.
Carry every open issue into the next year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a pre-disclosure correction date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the Section D test
actions: Compute the exception rate over the sample and compare it to the zero-unexplained-material-line threshold.
State the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - with the workpaper references that support it.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared no sampled valuation file or narrative paragraph, sign the workpaper and date it.
Report the conclusion and any open exceptions to the Audit Committee before it approves the SFCR, and file the workpaper in the financial reporting repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and Audit Committee reporting date is filed before SFCR approval.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns submission of the quantitative reporting templates, the RSR and the SFCR to each national competent authority; escalates any at-risk deadline to the Chief Financial Officer the day it is identified

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Directive 2009/138/EC Art. 48(1)(g)-(i) on the actuarial function's contribution to the risk management system, SCR/MCR modelling and the ORSA, read alongside Art. 35 supervisory reporting and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/894 for the templates and submission formats in force at the reference date

In-scope processes.value: Supervisory reporting cycle - template production, actuarial function confirmation of SCR and MCR inputs, EIOPA taxonomy validation, national competent authority submission and feedback handling - for every solo undertaking and the group

In-scope systems.value: Reporting engine that assembles the QRT set and generates the XBRL instance against the EIOPA taxonomy, with submission receipts and NCA feedback files stored against the reporting reference date

Compliance procedure documented.value: Supervisory Submission Procedure - template scope by reference date, taxonomy version control, blocking and non-blocking validation handling, actuarial function confirmation on SCR/MCR, AMSB approval, portal upload and receipt capture, resubmission rules

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Financial Officer and the Chief Risk Officer jointly, refreshed on every EIOPA taxonomy release and on any NCA reporting circular or national add-on change

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Quarterly solo templates within 5 weeks of quarter end and group within 11 weeks; annual solo templates and RSR within 14 weeks of 31 December and group within 20 weeks; the ORSA supervisory report within 2 weeks of the assessment being completed

Deadline reminders configured.value: Calendar alerts to the preparer, reviewer and approver at deadline minus 15, 7, 3 and 1 working days, with an automatic escalation to the CFO if the instance has not passed validation at deadline minus 3

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: XBRL instance file, validation report, actuarial function confirmation, AMSB approval minute, portal receipt with the submission identifier and the NCA feedback file retained 10 years by entity and reference date

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any submission made after the deadline, any rejected instance, and any resubmission is logged with the reference date, the cause of the miss, the days late and the corrective action

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The CFO signs off every late or rejected submission and every resubmission that changes a previously reported SCR, MCR or own-funds figure

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every supervisory submission due in the year across all solo entities and the group - four quarterly template sets, the annual template set, the RSR, the SFCR and any ORSA supervisory report - identified from the reporting calendar

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on lateness - any submission timestamped after the regulatory deadline is a fail; any instance submitted with an unresolved blocking validation error is a fail; more than two non-blocking errors left unexplained on a single instance is a fail

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly supervisory submission test workpaper - calendar extract, receipt-to-deadline comparison, validation report review and exception log - filed in the compliance evidence repository by reference date

Regulator-ready documentation.value: A submission register showing per entity and reference date the template set, the taxonomy version, the submission timestamp, the NCA submission identifier and the feedback status, producible within 5 working days of an NCA request

checklist.step: Open the reporting cycle and confirm the template scope for the reference date
actions: Open the reporting calendar entry for the reference date and list every entity in scope, including any branch and any third-country subsidiary consolidated into the group.

Determine the template set applicable at that reference date - quarterly sets are the reduced list (S.01, S.02.01, S.05.01, S.06.02, S.08.01, S.12.01, S.17.01, S.23.01, S.28), annual sets the full list.
Confirm with the national competent authority's reporting circular whether the entity has an approved exemption from quarterly reporting or from the item-by-item asset list.
Record any national add-on templates the NCA requires beyond the harmonised set and assign an owner to each.
Publish the cycle scope to the preparers, the actuarial function and the Controller as the definitive list.
checklist.done: the cycle scope names every entity, every harmonised template, every national add-on and an owner for each.

checklist.step: Pin the EIOPA taxonomy version and load the validation rule set
actions: Check the EIOPA taxonomy release page for the version applicable to the reference date and note the exact release number and its published start date.
Confirm the reporting engine is upgraded to that taxonomy release and that the previous release is retired so it cannot be selected by mistake.
Import the accompanying EIOPA validation rule set, separating blocking rules from non-blocking rules.
Run a smoke test on the prior period's instance under the new taxonomy to surface breaking changes before live data is loaded.
Record the taxonomy release number in the cycle file - it must appear in the submitted instance header.
checklist.done: the pinned taxonomy release is installed, its validation rules are loaded and a prior-period smoke test has been run against it.

checklist.step: Load balance sheet, own funds and capital figures into the templates
actions: Import the approved Solvency II balance sheet into S.02.01.02 and confirm it agrees to the excess of assets over liabilities used in own funds.
Populate S.23.01.01 with own-funds items by tier, applying the tiering limits, and confirm the eligible amounts to cover SCR and MCR.
Populate S.25.01, S.25.02 or S.25.03 depending on whether the standard formula, a partial internal model or a full internal model is used.
Populate S.28.01 or S.28.02 for the MCR and confirm the linear MCR sits inside the 25 percent floor and 45 percent cap of SCR and above the absolute floor for the entity's business.
Hand the populated set to the Chief Financial Officer's team for a figure-level review before validation.
checklist.done: balance sheet, own funds, SCR and MCR templates are populated, tiering limits applied and the MCR corridor tested.

checklist.step: Obtain the actuarial function's written confirmation of the SCR and MCR inputs
actions: Review the technical provisions, the risk-mitigation recognition and the underwriting-risk inputs feeding the SCR calculation for the reference date.
Confirm in writing that the actuarial function has contributed to the risk modelling underlying the SCR and MCR calculation as Art. 48(1)(g)-(i) requires, naming the models and runs relied on.
State any input the actuarial function could not verify and the consequence for the reported figure.
Where the reference date is an ORSA cycle date, confirm the same technical provisions basis feeds the ORSA projections so the two are reconcilable.
Send the signed confirmation to the Regulatory Reporting Manager for the submission evidence pack.
checklist.done: a signed actuarial function confirmation naming the models and runs behind the SCR and MCR sits in the evidence pack.

checklist.step: Generate the XBRL instance and run the EIOPA validation rules
actions: Generate the XBRL instance for each entity against the pinned taxonomy, with the correct entity LEI, reference date, currency and reporting basis in the header.
Run the full EIOPA validation suite and export the validation report listing every triggered rule with its identifier and severity.
Fix every blocking error at source in the underlying data rather than by overriding the cell, then regenerate and revalidate.
For each remaining non-blocking error write the business justification into the cycle file, since the NCA will ask for it in the feedback loop.
Save the clean validation report next to the instance file as the pre-submission evidence.
checklist.done: the instance carries the correct header data, no blocking errors remain, and every non-blocking error has a written justification.

checklist.step: Prepare the narrative reports required at this reference date
actions: For an annual reference date, assemble the Regular Supervisory Report covering business and performance, system of governance, risk profile, valuation and capital management.
Confirm whether the NCA has agreed a three-yearly full RSR with annual summaries, and prepare the version actually due this cycle.
Attach the SFCR approved by the administrative body and confirm the narrative figures tie to the instance being submitted.
Where an ORSA has been completed since the last submission, prepare the ORSA supervisory report for submission within two weeks of the assessment's completion date.
Convert each narrative to the file format the NCA portal accepts and check the file size against the portal limit.
checklist.done: every narrative report due at this reference date is assembled, tied to the instance and in the portal's accepted format.

checklist.step: Secure administrative body approval of the reported figures
actions: Circulate the SCR, MCR, own funds and coverage ratio summary with the actuarial function confirmation to the administrative, management or supervisory body.
Table the approval resolution for the submission and record any conditions the body attaches.
Where the cycle is quarterly and the body has delegated approval, confirm the delegation is in force and the delegate is named in the terms of reference.
Capture the signed resolution or delegated approval with its date into the submission evidence pack.
checklist.done: a dated approval - board resolution or documented delegation - covers the exact figures being submitted.

checklist.step: Verify portal credentials, entity identifiers and submitter rights
actions: Confirm each named submitter's account on the NCA reporting portal is active and that the certificate or multi-factor token has not expired inside the submission window.
Verify the entity LEI is current and not lapsed at the GLEIF register, since a lapsed LEI will fail the header validation.
Check the submitter is mapped to the correct entity and reporting role on the portal, and request the mapping from the NCA at least 10 working days before a first-time submission.
Keep a second trained submitter provisioned for every entity so a single absence cannot cause a missed deadline.
checklist.done: credentials, certificates, entity LEIs and portal role mappings are all valid for the whole submission window, with a backup submitter provisioned.

checklist.step: Upload the instance and the narratives to the supervisory portal
actions: Log in to the national competent authority's reporting portal and select the entity, the reporting framework and the reference date.
Upload the validated XBRL instance and attach the RSR, SFCR or ORSA supervisory report where the cycle requires them.
Submit no later than the working day before the regulatory deadline so a rejection can still be corrected inside the window.
Do not submit a partially populated instance to hold the date - a rejected or incomplete filing does not stop the clock.
checklist.done: the instance and its narratives are uploaded and submitted at least one working day before the regulatory deadline.

checklist.step: Capture the submission receipt and the identifier
actions: Download the portal acknowledgement showing the submission identifier, the entity, the reference date and the server timestamp.
Record the identifier and timestamp on the submission register row for that entity and reference date.
File the acknowledgement, the submitted instance and the validation report together so the three can be produced as one package.
Compare the timestamp to the regulatory deadline and mark the row On Time or Late - never leave it blank.
checklist.done: the register row carries the submission identifier, the timestamp, the on-time flag and links to the instance, validation report and acknowledgement.

checklist.step: Work the national competent authority feedback file
actions: Download the NCA feedback file when it is published and list every data-quality flag with its rule identifier and the cell it points at.
Assign each flag to the template owner with a response due date inside the NCA's stated response window.
Answer each flag either with a correction or with a written explanation of why the reported figure is right.
Record the response and the NCA's closure of the flag on the submission register row.
checklist.done: every NCA feedback flag has an owner, a dated response and a recorded closure.

checklist.step: Control resubmissions and record the reason for change
actions: Assess whether a discovered error crosses the resubmission threshold in the NCA's reporting circular, and default to resubmitting where SCR, MCR or own funds move.
Regenerate the instance from corrected source data, revalidate it and mark it as a resubmission for the same reference date.
Write the reason for change - what was wrong, what moved, by how much - and attach it to the resubmission.
Notify the NCA supervisory contact in writing where the correction changes a previously reported capital figure, rather than letting them find it.
Link the resubmission to the original register row so both versions remain traceable.
checklist.done: each resubmission carries a reason for change, a link to the original submission and, where capital figures moved, a written notification to the NCA.

checklist.step: Reconcile submitted figures across templates and against the prior period
actions: Reconcile own funds in S.23.01 to the excess of assets over liabilities in S.02.01.02 plus subordinated liabilities treated as own funds.
Reconcile the SCR in S.25 to the SCR used in the MCR corridor test in S.28 and to the coverage ratio reported to the board.
Run the variation analysis templates S.29.01 to S.29.04 for the annual cycle and explain the movement in the excess of assets over liabilities.
Compare every key figure to the prior reference date and write a driver for any movement above 10 percent before submission.
checklist.done: cross-template reconciliations tie and every key movement above 10 percent from the prior period has a written driver.

checklist.step: Escalate any submission at risk of missing its deadline
actions: At deadline minus 3 working days, list every entity whose instance has not yet passed validation.
Raise a tracker issue per at-risk entity naming the blocker, the owner and the earliest realistic submission time.
Escalate to the Chief Financial Officer the same day and agree whether to request an extension from the NCA in writing - extensions are granted before, never after, the deadline.
Where a deadline will be missed, notify the NCA supervisory contact in advance with the reason and the committed submission date.
checklist.done: every at-risk submission has a tracker issue, a same-day CFO escalation and, where the deadline will be missed, an advance written notification to the NCA.

checklist.step: Close the cycle and archive the submission evidence pack
actions: Confirm every entity in the cycle scope has a submission register row with an identifier, a timestamp and a feedback status.
Assemble the evidence pack per entity - instance file, validation report, actuarial confirmation, approval minute, acknowledgement, feedback responses.
Apply the 10-year retention label and index the pack by entity, reference date and submission identifier.
Report the cycle outcome - on-time percentage, rejections, resubmissions, open feedback flags - to the CFO and the Risk Committee.
checklist.done: every in-scope entity has an archived, indexed evidence pack and the cycle outcome has been reported to the CFO and Risk Committee.

testing.step: Build the population of submissions that were due in the period
actions: Extract from the reporting calendar every submission obligation with a due date in the period, by entity, reference date and report type.
Rebuild the expected obligation list independently from the group legal-entity register so an entity omitted from the calendar cannot hide.
Compare the two lists and investigate every difference before sampling - a missing calendar row is itself an exception.
Sign the reconciled population as complete with the extraction date and source versions.
testing.done: the calendar population is reconciled to the legal-entity register with every difference investigated, and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile every due submission to a portal acknowledgement
actions: Match each population row to a submission register row carrying a portal submission identifier and a server timestamp.
Reject register rows evidenced only by an internal note, an email or a screenshot of the upload screen - only the portal acknowledgement counts.
List unmatched obligations as automatic exceptions with no judgement applied.
Confirm resubmissions are linked to their original rows and not counted as separate obligations.
testing.done: every due submission matches a portal acknowledgement with an identifier and timestamp, or is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Recompute the regulatory deadline for each submission and test timeliness
actions: Recompute the deadline from the reference date - 5 weeks for solo quarterly, 11 weeks for group quarterly, 14 weeks for solo annual, 20 weeks for group annual, 2 weeks from completion for the ORSA supervisory report.
Apply the NCA's stated treatment of weekends and national public holidays rather than assuming calendar days.
Compare each acknowledgement timestamp to the recomputed deadline and compute the days early or late.
Treat every late submission as a fail and confirm whether an advance written extension existed.
testing.done: every submission has an independently recomputed deadline, a computed days-early figure and a fail flag where it was late.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of submissions for deep testing
actions: Take 100 percent of annual submissions, 100 percent of late or resubmitted filings and 100 percent of first-time entity submissions.
Take 12 quarterly submissions by seeded random selection across entities and quarters.
Record the seed, the strata, the population size and the selection date so the sample can be redrawn.
Confirm the sample spans at least three national competent authorities where the group reports to more than one.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all annual, late, resubmitted and first-time filings, and spans multiple NCAs.

testing.step: Re-run the EIOPA validation suite on each sampled instance
actions: Retrieve the exact instance file that was submitted, not a regenerated copy, and confirm its hash matches the archived version.
Re-run the EIOPA validation rules for the taxonomy release named in the instance header.
Confirm no blocking rule fires and compare the non-blocking results to the justifications recorded at submission time.
Confirm the header LEI, reference date, currency and taxonomy release match the entity and cycle - a mismatched header means the wrong instance was filed.
testing.done: each sampled instance revalidates with no blocking errors, a correct header, and non-blocking errors matched to recorded justifications.

testing.step: Re-perform the MCR corridor and own-funds eligibility maths
actions: Recompute the linear MCR from S.28 inputs and test it against the 25 percent floor and 45 percent cap of the reported SCR.
Confirm the absolute floor for the entity's business type was applied where the corridor result falls below it.
Recompute eligible own funds after tier limits - Tier 1 at least 50 percent of SCR, Tier 3 no more than 15 percent of SCR, and Tier 2 plus Tier 3 no more than 50 percent.
Compare the recomputed SCR and MCR coverage ratios to the figures reported to the NCA and to the board.
testing.done: the MCR corridor, absolute floor and own-funds tier limits are independently recomputed and agree to the submitted figures.

testing.step: Trace the actuarial function confirmation behind each sampled SCR
actions: Pull the actuarial function confirmation for each sampled reference date and check it is signed and dated before the submission timestamp.
Confirm it names the specific model runs relied on and that those run identifiers exist in the actuarial platform.
Confirm any input the actuarial function flagged as unverified was resolved or disclosed rather than silently submitted.
Treat a confirmation dated after submission, or a generic confirmation naming no run, as a fail.
testing.done: each sampled SCR is supported by a pre-dated, run-specific actuarial function confirmation.

testing.step: Test approval, credentials and segregation on the sampled submissions
actions: Confirm a board resolution or a documented delegation approved the exact figures submitted, dated before the submission timestamp.
Pull the portal submitter identity from the acknowledgement and confirm the submitter was not also the sole preparer of the instance.
Check portal access entitlements against the identity platform for joiners and leavers - a departed employee retaining submitter rights is an exception.
Confirm a backup submitter was provisioned for each entity during the window.
testing.done: every sampled submission has a pre-dated approval, a submitter segregated from the preparer, and clean portal entitlements.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception naming the entity, the reference date, the report type and the days late or the failed rule.
Assign a root cause from the standard set - source data late, taxonomy upgrade missed, credential expired, validation error unresolved, approval not obtained, calendar row missing.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and open a self-report assessment with the Regulatory Reporting Manager for any missed statutory deadline.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the submission test
actions: Compute the on-time submission rate and the validation failure rate and compare them to the zero-tolerance threshold.
State the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - with the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared, validated or uploaded no sampled submission, sign and date the workpaper.
Report results and any missed deadlines to the Risk Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, on-time rate and Risk Committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the annual-only quantitative reporting templates - asset list, premiums and claims by line of business and by country, claims development triangles, own funds, SCR risk modules, reinsurance and variation analysis - for every solo entity and the group

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Directive 2009/138/EC Art. 48(1)(g)-(i) on the actuarial function's contribution to SCR and MCR modelling, read with Art. 35 supervisory reporting and the annual template specifications and log files of the Implementing Technical Standards on reporting in force at the 31 December reference date

In-scope processes.value: Annual supervisory reporting - preparation of the annual-only templates S.05, S.06.02, S.08, S.09, S.19.01, S.23.01, S.25, S.26, S.27.01, S.29, S.30, S.31 and, for the group, S.32 to S.37 - sourced from the investment book of record, the policy and claims systems and the actuarial platform

In-scope systems.value: Warehouse layer where the asset-by-asset holdings, premium and claim transactions and reinsurance recoverables are conformed to Solvency II lines of business, CIC codes and country of underwriting before templating

Compliance procedure documented.value: Annual QRT Preparation Procedure - template-by-template source mapping, CIC and complementary identification code assignment rules, line-of-business allocation rules, triangle construction basis, cross-template validation set and the sign-off matrix

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Financial Officer with the Chief Actuary countersigning the actuarial-sourced templates; re-approved each year before the annual pack opens and on any change to the template log files

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual templates for solo undertakings due within 14 weeks of the 31 December reference date and for the group within 20 weeks; the asset list and triangle templates must be data-complete by year-end plus 6 weeks to leave room for cross-template validation

Deadline reminders configured.value: One milestone per template owner at year-end plus 4, 6, 9 and 12 weeks, with the asset list and the claims triangles carrying the earliest milestones because they drive downstream templates

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Source extracts, CIC and line-of-business mapping tables, triangle construction workings, template-owner sign-offs and cross-template validation results retained 10 years by entity and reporting year

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any template submitted with an unmapped CIC code, an unallocated line of business, a triangle that does not reconcile to the reserving data, or a failed cross-template check is logged with owner and correction date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The CFO signs off any annual template restated after submission and any change to the line-of-business allocation rules that moves reported premium or claims between segments

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every annual-only template instance submitted for the reporting year across all solo entities and the group, together with the source populations behind them - the full year-end holdings file, the premium and claims transaction sets and the reinsurance recoverable ledger

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero unmapped CIC codes and zero unallocated lines of business; S.05.01 premiums must agree to the audited technical account within 0.5 percent; every claims triangle must reconcile to the reserving data with no unexplained residual; any failed cross-template validation is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is annual, so the test runs once on the year-end pack, with a dry run of the asset list and line-of-business mappings on the 30 September data to surface mapping gaps before the year-end crunch

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside statutory and actuarial reporting and must not have prepared, mapped or signed off any sampled template

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual QRT test workpaper - source reconciliations, mapping coverage tests, triangle re-performance, cross-template validation rerun and exception log - filed in the financial reporting repository under the reporting year

Regulator-ready documentation.value: A per-template source-to-cell traceability pack showing extract, transformation rule and template cell, producible to the national competent authority within 10 working days of a data-quality query

Regulator response path.value: The Statutory Reporting Manager answers NCA template queries; the Chief Actuary clears any answer touching triangles, technical provisions or SCR risk modules, and material misstatement triggers a resubmission notified in advance

checklist.step: Open the annual pack and list every annual-only template in scope
actions: List the annual-only templates due for each entity: S.05.01 and S.05.02 premiums claims and expenses by line of business and by country, S.06.02 list of assets, S.08.01 derivatives, S.09.01 income gains and losses, S.19.01 non-life claims triangles, S.23.01 own funds, S.25 SCR, S.26.01 to S.26.07 risk modules, S.27.01 catastrophe risk, S.29.01 to S.29.04 variation analysis, S.30 and S.31 reinsurance.

Add the group-only templates S.32.01 undertakings in scope, S.33.01 individual requirements, S.34.01 other regulated undertakings, S.36.01 to S.36.04 intra-group transactions and S.37.01 risk concentration.
Strike out templates the entity is genuinely out of scope for - S.19.01 for a pure life entity, S.27.01 where no catastrophe risk module applies - and record why for each.
Assign a named preparer and a named reviewer to every remaining template and publish the matrix.
checklist.done: every annual-only and group template has a preparer, a reviewer or a documented out-of-scope reason.

checklist.step: Build the item-by-item asset list for S.06.02 with CIC codes and identifiers
actions: Extract every holding at 31 December with ISIN, quantity, par amount, unit price, accrued interest, Solvency II value, acquisition value, currency, custodian and issuer.
Assign the four-character CIC code to each holding - first two characters the country of listing or XL for not listed, last two the asset category - and reject any holding left unmapped.
Populate issuer name, issuer LEI, issuer sector on the NACE classification and issuer group for concentration analysis.
Apply the look-through to collective investment undertakings and populate S.06.03 with the underlying asset categories, countries and currencies.
Reconcile the total Solvency II value on the asset list to the investment lines of S.02.01.02 and clear any difference before release.
checklist.done: every holding carries a CIC code, an issuer LEI and a NACE sector, look-through is applied, and the list totals tie to the balance sheet.

checklist.step: Complete the derivatives and investment income templates
actions: Populate S.08.01 for open derivative positions with notional amount, buyer or seller position, counterparty name and LEI, trigger value, maturity date and Solvency II value.
Populate S.08.02 for derivatives closed during the year with the realised gain or loss.
Confirm each derivative flagged as risk mitigation meets the effectiveness conditions relied on in the SCR calculation and mark those rows for the actuarial reviewer.
Populate S.09.01 with dividends, interest, rent and net gains and losses by asset category and reconcile the total to the investment income line of the audited income statement.
checklist.done: open and closed derivative positions are reported with counterparty LEIs, and S.09.01 investment income ties to the audited income statement.

checklist.step: Allocate premiums, claims and expenses to Solvency II lines of business
actions: Extract the year's written premium, earned premium, claims incurred, changes in other technical provisions and expenses incurred at policy or contract level.
Map each contract to its Solvency II line of business using the standing product-to-LoB mapping table, including the proportional and non-proportional reinsurance lines.
Populate S.05.01 gross direct, gross proportional reinsurance accepted, gross non-proportional accepted, reinsurers' share and net, per line of business.
Populate S.05.02 by country - the home country plus the five countries with the largest gross written premium, with the remainder aggregated.
Reconcile total gross written premium and claims incurred to the audited technical account and explain any difference above 0.5 percent.
checklist.done: every contract is allocated to a line of business, S.05.01 and S.05.02 are populated, and totals agree to the audited technical account within 0.5 percent.

checklist.step: Construct the non-life claims development triangles
actions: Build gross claims paid, gross undiscounted best estimate claims provisions and gross reported but not settled triangles by accident or underwriting year, on the basis the entity has consistently adopted, for the required development years.
Populate S.19.01 for each material non-life line of business and for the total, in the reporting currency and, where required, by significant currency.
Reconcile the latest diagonal of the paid triangle to the claims paid in the year reported in S.05.01.
Reconcile the closing best estimate on the triangle to the non-life technical provisions in S.17.01 and explain any difference such as ENID loadings or discounting.
Note the basis - accident year or underwriting year - in the template header, since a basis change between years must be flagged.
checklist.done: each triangle reconciles to S.05.01 paid claims and to the S.17.01 best estimate, on a stated and consistent accident or underwriting year basis.

checklist.step: Populate the own funds template with tiering and restrictions
actions: Populate S.23.01.01 with ordinary share capital, share premium, the reconciliation reserve, subordinated liabilities and any ancillary own funds approved by the NCA.
Classify each item into Tier 1 unrestricted, Tier 1 restricted, Tier 2 or Tier 3 using the Delegated Regulation classification criteria and grandfathering where applicable.
Compute the reconciliation reserve as excess of assets over liabilities less foreseeable dividends, own shares, restricted own funds in ring-fenced funds and other basic own-fund items.
Apply the eligibility limits separately against SCR and MCR and populate the eligible own-funds rows.
Populate S.23.02 to S.23.04 where the group structure requires the detailed own-funds and reconciliation-reserve breakdowns.
checklist.done: own funds are tiered, the reconciliation reserve is computed with all deductions, and eligibility limits are applied separately to SCR and MCR.

checklist.step: Populate the SCR risk module templates from the calculation kernel
actions: Export the standard formula results by module and sub-module and populate S.26.01 market risk, S.26.02 counterparty default, S.26.03 life underwriting, S.26.04 health underwriting, S.26.05 non-life underwriting, S.26.06 operational risk and S.26.07 simplifications used.
Confirm the diversification benefit and the loss-absorbing capacity of technical provisions and deferred taxes reported in S.25.01 tie to the module sums.
Populate S.27.01 catastrophe risk with natural catastrophe scenarios by peril and country, man-made catastrophe scenarios and the aggregation.
Where a partial or full internal model is used, populate S.25.02 or S.25.03 instead and confirm the model version matches the approved model documentation reference.
Have the actuarial function confirm in writing that it contributed to the risk modelling behind these figures, as Art. 48(1)(g)-(i) requires.
checklist.done: every SCR risk-module template is populated, ties to the S.25 aggregate, and carries a written actuarial function contribution statement.

checklist.step: Prepare the variation analysis templates
actions: Populate S.29.01 with the movement in the excess of assets over liabilities from the prior year-end to this year-end, split into its analysed components.
Populate S.29.02 with the variation due to investments and financial liabilities and S.29.03 with the variation due to technical provisions.
Populate S.29.04 with the detailed analysis by period and by line of business, splitting the technical flows of the year from the change in provisions for prior years.
Confirm the analysed components sum exactly to the total movement in excess of assets over liabilities - an unexplained residual is not acceptable in this template family.
Write a short driver narrative for each component above the materiality floor, for use in the RSR.
checklist.done: the variation analysis components sum exactly to the movement in excess of assets over liabilities with a driver narrative on each material component.

checklist.step: Populate the reinsurance templates and check facultative coverage
actions: Populate S.30.01 and S.30.02 with facultative covers for the ten largest risks per line of business, showing the risk identification code, sum insured, ceded share and reinsurer.
Populate S.30.03 and S.30.04 with outgoing reinsurance programme data by treaty - type, layer, attachment point, limit, reinstatements, estimated ceded premium.
Populate S.31.01 with the share of reinsurers, including reinsurer name, LEI, credit quality step and the reinsurance recoverables balance.
Populate S.31.02 for special purpose vehicles where any risk is transferred to one.
Reconcile total reinsurance recoverables in S.31.01 to the recoverables line in S.02.01.02 and to the ceded ledger.
checklist.done: facultative, treaty and reinsurer-share templates are populated with LEIs and credit quality steps, and recoverables tie to the balance sheet.

checklist.step: Prepare the group-specific templates
actions: Populate S.32.01 with every undertaking in the scope of the group, its LEI, country, type, supervisory authority, and the method used for group solvency.
Populate S.33.01 with individual requirements for insurance and reinsurance undertakings and S.34.01 for other regulated and non-regulated undertakings.

Populate S.36.01 to S.36.04 with intra-group transactions - equity type, debt and asset transfer, derivatives, internal reinsurance and cost sharing - above the reporting threshold agreed with the group supervisor.
Populate S.37.01 with risk concentration by counterparty and exposure type against the same agreed threshold.
Confirm the group scope agrees to the legal-entity register and that entities acquired or disposed during the year are treated on the correct basis.
checklist.done: the group templates are populated, the scope agrees to the legal-entity register, and intra-group transactions and concentrations are reported against the agreed thresholds.

checklist.step: Run the cross-template validation set before release
actions: Run the full EIOPA validation suite across the assembled annual pack, not template by template, so cross-template rules actually fire.

Check the standing internal cross-checks: S.06.02 total to S.02.01.02 investments, S.05.01 claims paid to the S.19.01 latest diagonal, S.31.01 recoverables to S.02.01.02, S.25 SCR to S.28 corridor, S.29.01 movement to the change in R0700.
Fix differences in the source data rather than by hard-coding the template cell, and regenerate.
Export the clean validation report and attach it to the annual pack as the pre-release evidence.
checklist.done: the full pack passes the EIOPA validation suite and every standing internal cross-check, with a clean validation report attached.

checklist.step: Collect template-owner sign-offs against the sign-off matrix
actions: Circulate each template to its named preparer and reviewer for a dated sign-off stating the source system, the extraction date and any known limitation.
Require the Chief Actuary's countersignature on S.19.01, S.25, S.26, S.27.01 and S.29.03.
Require the Chief Investment Officer's countersignature on S.06.02, S.08 and S.09.01.
Chase any template without both a preparer and a reviewer signature - an unsigned template cannot enter the submission pack.
checklist.done: every template carries a dated preparer and reviewer sign-off plus the required functional countersignature.

checklist.step: Document the mapping tables used to produce the pack
actions: Version and publish the product-to-line-of-business mapping, the CIC assignment rules and the country-of-underwriting rules used for this reporting year.
Record every change from the prior year with its rationale and its quantified effect on reported premium, claims or asset categories.
Register each mapping table in the data catalogue with an owner, a review date and a link to the templates it feeds.
Publish the mapping change log to the Chief Financial Officer and the Chief Actuary before the pack is submitted.
checklist.done: every mapping table is versioned, catalogued with an owner, and each change from prior year is quantified and communicated.

checklist.step: Release the annual pack into the submission cycle
actions: Confirm every in-scope template is present, signed and validation-clean, then lock the pack against further edits.
Hand the locked pack to the submission process with the validation report, the sign-off matrix and the mapping change log.
Confirm the pack is released by year-end plus 12 weeks for solo and plus 18 weeks for group so the submitter has buffer against the 14 and 20 week deadlines.
Record the release date and the pack version on the reporting calendar entry.
checklist.done: a locked, signed, validation-clean pack is released with buffer ahead of the 14-week solo and 20-week group deadlines.

checklist.step: Archive the source extracts and workings behind every template
actions: Archive each template's source extract with its extraction timestamp, the query or job identifier and the record count.
Archive the triangle workings, the CIC mapping output, the line-of-business allocation output and the cross-template validation report.
Build the source-to-cell traceability index so any reported cell can be walked back to its extract in one hop.
Apply the 10-year retention label and index by entity, reporting year and template code.
checklist.done: each template's source extract and workings are archived, indexed by template code, and traceable cell-to-extract in one hop.

testing.step: Build the population of annual templates and their source records
actions: List every annual-only and group template submitted for the reporting year by entity, and every template marked out of scope with its stated reason.
Independently pull the year-end holdings count, the premium transaction count and the claims transaction count from the source systems.
Reconcile the source counts to the record counts archived with each template extract and investigate any difference.
Sign the population as complete, recording the pull date and the source system versions.
testing.done: the template population and the underlying source record counts are reconciled and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the templates to the audited financial statements
actions: Agree S.05.01 total gross written premium and claims incurred to the audited technical account and compute the difference as a percentage.
Agree S.09.01 investment income to the audited income statement investment result.
Agree S.06.02 total Solvency II value to the investment lines of S.02.01.02 and to the audited investment note adjusted for the valuation bridge.
Treat any difference above 0.5 percent without a documented driver as an exception.
testing.done: premium, claims and investment totals agree to the audited statements within 0.5 percent or the difference is documented and quantified.

testing.step: Test mapping coverage on the asset list and the line-of-business allocation
actions: Run a completeness query for null or default CIC codes, null issuer LEIs and null NACE sectors across the whole S.06.02 population, not a sample.
Run the same completeness test for unallocated lines of business across the whole premium and claims population.
Re-derive 30 CIC codes independently from the instrument's listing country and asset category and compare to the assigned code.
Report the coverage percentage and list every unmapped or defaulted record as an exception.
testing.done: CIC, LEI, NACE and line-of-business coverage is tested across the full population with every unmapped record listed.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of templates and records
actions: Take 100 percent of the templates carrying an actuarial countersignature and 100 percent of templates whose mapping rules changed this year.
Take 40 holdings from S.06.02, 25 contracts from the S.05.01 population and 10 treaties from S.30.03 by seeded random selection.
Record the seed, the strata, the population sizes and the selection date so the sample can be redrawn.
Confirm the sample spans every material line of business and both life and non-life where the entity writes both.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible from a recorded seed and spans all material lines of business and all changed-mapping templates.

testing.step: Re-perform the claims development triangles
actions: Rebuild the gross paid triangle for two sampled lines of business directly from the claims transaction extract without using the submitted template.
Compare the rebuilt latest diagonal to the paid claims reported in S.05.01 for the same line.
Compare the rebuilt closing best estimate column to the S.17.01 best estimate and confirm the stated reconciling items - ENID, discounting, expenses - explain the whole difference.
Confirm the accident or underwriting year basis matches the basis used in the prior year, and quantify the effect if it changed.
testing.done: two independently rebuilt triangles agree to S.05.01 paid claims and to S.17.01 with every reconciling item explained.

testing.step: Re-perform the own-funds tiering and reconciliation reserve
actions: Recompute the reconciliation reserve from excess of assets over liabilities less foreseeable dividends, own shares, ring-fenced fund restrictions and other basic own-fund items.
Re-classify each own-funds item against the Delegated Regulation tier criteria without reference to the submitted classification.
Recompute eligible own funds against SCR and against MCR separately and compare to S.23.01.01.
Confirm foreseeable dividends deducted match the dividend actually proposed to shareholders in the board minute.
testing.done: the reconciliation reserve, tiering and eligibility limits are independently recomputed and agree to the submitted own-funds template.

testing.step: Trace sampled holdings and contracts to source and to reported cells
actions: For each sampled holding, pull the custodian statement or the investment system record and agree ISIN, quantity, price, accrued interest and Solvency II value to the S.06.02 row.
For each sampled contract, pull the policy record and agree the line-of-business allocation, the country of underwriting and the premium amount to the S.05 population.
For each sampled treaty, pull the treaty document and agree the attachment point, limit, reinstatements and ceded share to S.30.03.
Capture the source screen or document reference for every traced item into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled holding, contract and treaty traces to a source document with all reported attributes agreeing.

testing.step: Re-run the cross-template validation set independently
actions: Re-run the EIOPA validation suite over the submitted pack as filed and compare the result to the validation report archived at release.

Independently recompute the standing cross-checks - S.06.02 to S.02.01.02, S.05.01 to S.19.01 diagonal, S.31.01 to S.02.01.02 recoverables, S.26 modules to S.25 aggregate, S.29.01 to the movement in R0700.
Confirm the S.29 components sum exactly to the movement in excess of assets over liabilities with no residual.
List any check that fails on rerun but passed at release, which indicates the pack changed after validation.
testing.done: the independent revalidation reproduces the release result and every standing cross-check recomputes without residual.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the entity, the template code, the affected cell or record and the amount involved.
Assign a root cause from the standard set - unmapped CIC, stale mapping table, triangle basis change undocumented, extract taken before close, cross-check skipped, sign-off missing.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and assess whether the error crosses the resubmission threshold with the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
Carry every open issue into next year's annual test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a resubmission assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the annual template test
actions: Compute the exception rate by template family and compare it to the zero-unmapped and 0.5 percent reconciliation thresholds.
State the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - with the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared or signed off no sampled template, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and open exceptions to the Audit Committee and file the workpaper in the financial reporting repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate by template family and Audit Committee reporting date is filed.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the external audit of the annual accounts and of the audited elements of the SFCR, and the interface with the internal audit function that evaluates the internal control system under Art. 47

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Directive 2009/138/EC Art. 47(1)-(2) on an effective, objective and independent internal audit function, read with Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Art. 271 on internal audit policy, plan, reporting and freedom from operational influence, and the national competent authority's rule on external audit of SFCR elements

In-scope processes.value: Annual external audit cycle over the statutory financial statements and the audited elements of the SFCR, plus the internal audit function's annual evaluation of the internal control system and the other elements of the system of governance

In-scope systems.value: Audit workflow platform holding the internal audit universe, the risk-based annual plan, engagement workpapers, findings, management actions and the audit committee reporting pack

Compliance procedure documented.value: Audit Coordination Procedure - external audit scoping and timetable, the prepared-by-client schedule, management representation, adjustment handling and opinion filing; and the Internal Audit Charter setting independence, unrestricted access, direct board reporting and the prohibition on auditing work the auditor performed

Compliance procedure approved.value: The Internal Audit Charter is approved by the administrative body on the Audit Committee's recommendation and reviewed annually; the external audit plan is approved by the Audit Committee before fieldwork opens

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: External audit opinion on the annual accounts required before the accounts are laid and before the SFCR is disclosed at year-end plus 14 weeks solo; the internal audit annual report and plan go to the administrative body at least annually per Art. 271(4)

Deadline reminders configured.value: Audit timetable milestones at year-end minus 6 weeks for planning, plus 4 weeks for the PBC pack, plus 9 weeks for draft opinion and plus 12 weeks for signature, each alerting the Controller and the engagement partner contact

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Engagement letter, audit plan, PBC pack, management representation letter, summary of unadjusted differences, signed audit report, internal audit charter, annual plan and findings retained 10 years in the financial reporting repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Audit findings, unadjusted differences above the trivial threshold, internal control deficiencies and any restriction on the internal auditor's access are logged with severity, owner and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The Chief Audit Executive validates closure of every internal audit finding and confirms to the Audit Committee that management actions were implemented as described, not merely reported as done

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: The full external audit cycle for the reporting year plus every internal audit engagement completed in the year, every finding raised and every management action recorded as closed

Pass/fail thresholds.value: A modified or qualified opinion, an audit report signed after the SFCR disclosure date, an internal audit engagement performed by someone who owned the audited process, or a finding closed without validated evidence, is each a fail; unadjusted differences above performance materiality must be individually justified

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is annual, so the test runs once per audit cycle after the opinion is signed, with a mid-year check that the internal audit plan is on track and that independence attestations are current

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer acts for the Audit Committee and must be outside both the finance function and the internal audit function whose independence is being tested
