Evidence location for test results.value: Annual audit coordination test workpaper - timetable adherence, adjustment log review, independence attestation review and finding-closure re-performance - filed in the financial reporting repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Signed audit report, audit findings letter, internal audit charter, risk-based annual plan, engagement reports and the Audit Committee minutes recording them, producible to the national competent authority within 5 working days

Regulator response path.value: The Chief Audit Executive answers NCA questions on internal audit effectiveness and independence; the Chief Financial Officer answers on the external audit, and any auditor resignation or opinion modification is notified to the NCA without delay

checklist.step: Confirm the auditor appointment and the independence position
actions: Confirm the statutory auditor's appointment is current, records the engagement period, and complies with the mandatory firm rotation and tendering rules applying to public-interest entities.
Obtain the audit firm's written independence confirmation, including the list of non-audit services provided and the fee cap position against the audit fee.
Table the confirmation at the Audit Committee and record the committee's approval of any permitted non-audit service before it is engaged.
File the appointment resolution, the engagement letter and the independence confirmation in the board portal.
checklist.done: a current appointment, an engagement letter and a dated independence confirmation with the non-audit service position are on file and tabled at the Audit Committee.

checklist.step: Agree the audit scope including the audited elements of the SFCR
actions: Confirm with the national competent authority's rule which SFCR elements fall in audit scope - typically the Solvency II balance sheet, own funds and the valuation narrative - and whether technical provisions are covered by an actuarial specialist.
Agree materiality and performance materiality for the financial statements and, separately, for the SFCR elements, and record both figures.
Agree the significant risk areas - technical provisions, investment valuation, deferred tax recoverability, going concern - and the planned response to each.
Confirm which components of the group are in scope for full audit, specified procedures or review, and how component auditors report to the group engagement team.
Record the agreed scope in the audit plan and table it at the Audit Committee before fieldwork opens.
checklist.done: the audit plan states scope, materiality for both the accounts and the SFCR elements, significant risks and component coverage, and is Audit Committee approved.

checklist.step: Build and deliver the prepared-by-client pack against the timetable
actions: Take the auditor's PBC list and turn each request into a task with a named preparer, a due date and the source system it comes from.
Deliver the core schedules first - trial balance, lead schedules, investment holdings with valuations, technical provisions analysis, reinsurance recoverables ageing, related party listing.
Upload each item to the shared audit workspace with a version and a preparer name, never by loose email attachment.
Track the delivery percentage daily during fieldwork and escalate any item more than two days late to the Controller.
checklist.done: every PBC item is delivered with a named preparer and version into the shared audit workspace against the agreed dates.

checklist.step: Support the walkthroughs and controls testing over the reporting process
actions: Provide current process narratives and control descriptions for the close, valuation, technical provisions and supervisory reporting processes.
Arrange walkthrough sessions with each control owner and provide the population and the sample evidence the auditor requests.
Where a control has changed during the year, provide the change date and the evidence for both the pre-change and post-change periods.
Log every control deficiency the auditor raises with its severity, the compensating control if any, and the owner.
checklist.done: walkthroughs are completed for each in-scope process and every deficiency raised is logged with severity and owner.

checklist.step: Manage audit adjustments and the summary of unadjusted differences
actions: Log each proposed adjustment with the account, the amount, the direction, the audit basis and whether it affects the IFRS accounts, the Solvency II balance sheet or both.
Post accepted adjustments in the general ledger before the ledger is finally closed, and push the Solvency II effect through the valuation bridge.
For each declined adjustment write management's reasoning and confirm the aggregate of unadjusted differences stays below performance materiality on both bases.
Table the summary of unadjusted differences at the Audit Committee with management's rationale for each.
checklist.done: every adjustment is posted or declined with written reasoning, and the aggregate unadjusted difference is below performance materiality on both bases.

checklist.step: Sign the management representation letter
actions: Read the representation letter line by line against the evidence held, particularly on completeness of liabilities, litigation and claims, related party transactions and subsequent events.
Add the representations specific to Solvency II - completeness of technical provisions data, appropriateness of the valuation bases and the LTG measures applied.
Confirm the letter is dated no earlier than the date of the audit report and signed by both the CFO and the Chief Executive Officer.
File the signed letter with the audit evidence.
checklist.done: a signed representation letter dated no earlier than the audit report, covering the Solvency II specific representations, is on file.

checklist.step: Obtain and read the audit opinion and the findings letter
actions: Obtain the signed audit report on the annual accounts and the separate report or opinion on the audited elements of the SFCR.

Read the opinion wording for modification, emphasis of matter, material uncertainty related to going concern or key audit matters, and escalate any modification to the CFO and the Audit Committee the same day.
Obtain the audit findings letter and log every recommendation with an owner and a target date.
Confirm the audit report date precedes the SFCR disclosure date so the audited elements are covered when they are published.
checklist.done: a signed opinion on the accounts and on the audited SFCR elements exists, dated before disclosure, with every finding logged and owned.

checklist.step: Table the audit outcome at the Audit Committee
actions: Circulate the audit report, findings letter, summary of unadjusted differences and the auditor's independence confirmation at least 10 working days before the meeting.
Hold a session with the auditor without management present, as the committee's terms of reference require, and minute that it took place.
Record the committee's recommendation that the board approve the accounts and the SFCR.
Record each audit finding as a tracked action with an owner and a target date in the committee's action log.
checklist.done: the Audit Committee has considered the opinion and findings, held the auditor-only session, and recorded a recommendation and an action log.

checklist.step: File and publish the audited financial statements
actions: File the audited annual accounts with the national companies registry within the statutory filing period for the jurisdiction of incorporation.
Submit the audited accounts and the auditor's report to the national competent authority alongside the annual supervisory reporting pack.
Publish the annual report where the entity has a publication obligation and record the publication date and location.
Archive the signed accounts, the opinion and the filing receipts in the financial reporting repository under the reporting year.
checklist.done: audited accounts are filed with the registry and the NCA, published where required, and the receipts are archived.

checklist.step: Confirm the internal audit function's independence position
actions: Re-confirm that the internal audit function reports functionally to the administrative body and has unrestricted access to records, premises and staff, as Art. 271 requires.
Collect an annual independence and conflicts attestation from every internal auditor, naming any process they previously owned.
Confirm no internal auditor was assigned to an engagement covering a process they operated within the cooling-off period set in the charter.
Report any restriction on scope or access, or any pressure on findings, directly to the Audit Committee - Art. 47(2) makes this reportable.
checklist.done: independence attestations are current for every auditor, no self-review assignment occurred, and any scope restriction is reported to the committee.

checklist.step: Approve the risk-based internal audit plan
actions: Refresh the audit universe from the process inventory, the risk register and the outsourcing register so every material activity appears.
Score each auditable entity on inherent risk and control maturity and rank the universe.
Build the annual plan covering all major activities over a reasonable period, with explicit coverage of the system of governance elements - risk management, compliance, actuarial and outsourcing.
Present the plan and the resourcing assumption to the Audit Committee for approval and record the approval date.
Track plan completion monthly and take any material plan change back to the committee rather than absorbing it silently.
checklist.done: a risk-ranked annual plan covering the system of governance elements is approved by the Audit Committee with tracked completion.

checklist.step: Execute internal audit engagements and raise findings
actions: For each engagement, agree terms of reference with the auditee, document the control objectives and design the test programme before fieldwork.
Perform the testing, retain the evidence in the workpaper file and have the engagement lead review and sign every workpaper.
Rate each finding on the standard severity scale, agree the root cause with the auditee and obtain a management action with a named owner and a date.
Issue the engagement report to the auditee's executive and to the Audit Committee, and escalate any finding the auditee refuses to accept.
checklist.done: each engagement has terms of reference, reviewed workpapers, rated findings with agreed management actions, and an issued report.

checklist.step: Validate closure of findings rather than accepting a status update
actions: For every action management marks complete, request the evidence that the control now operates - a sample of executions, a system configuration screen, an approved procedure.
Re-test at least one instance of the remediated control before moving the finding to Closed.
Return to Open, with a new date, any action whose evidence does not demonstrate operation, and report repeat slippage to the Audit Committee.
Report the ageing profile of open findings by severity at every committee meeting.
checklist.done: no finding is closed without re-tested evidence of the control operating, and the open-finding ageing profile is reported each meeting.

checklist.step: Report internal audit results and an annual opinion to the administrative body
actions: Prepare the annual internal audit report covering plan completion, significant findings, thematic weaknesses and the status of prior-year actions.
State an overall opinion on the adequacy and effectiveness of the internal control system and the other elements of the system of governance, as Art. 47(1) frames the function's remit.
Present the report to the administrative body and record the body's determination of what action to take on each significant finding, which Art. 47(2) requires.
Log the body's decisions and monitor their implementation as a standing agenda item.
checklist.done: an annual internal audit report with an overall opinion is presented, and the administrative body's decisions on each significant finding are minuted and tracked.

checklist.step: Archive the audit evidence for both functions
actions: Archive the external audit set - engagement letter, plan, PBC pack, adjustments log, representation letter, signed opinion, findings letter, committee minutes.
Archive the internal audit set - charter, approved plan, engagement reports, workpaper index, findings and closure evidence, annual report.
Apply the 10-year retention label and index by reporting year, engagement and finding reference.
Confirm the internal audit archive is accessible to the Audit Committee and to the national competent authority on request without going through the audited functions.
checklist.done: both audit evidence sets are archived under a 10-year label, indexed by engagement, and reachable without passing through the audited function.

testing.step: Build the population of audit activity for the year
actions: Extract every internal audit engagement with a report date in the year, every finding raised and every action closed.
Add the external audit cycle - engagement letter, plan, opinion, findings letter and committee papers - as its own population block.
Reconcile the engagement list to the board-approved annual plan and list every planned engagement not delivered.
Sign the population as complete with the extraction date.
testing.done: the audit population reconciles to the approved plan with every undelivered engagement listed, and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile plan coverage to the audit universe and the system of governance
actions: Compare the audit universe to the process inventory, the risk register and the outsourcing register and list any material activity absent from the universe.
Confirm the plan covers the risk management, compliance, actuarial and outsourcing functions within the stated cycle length.
Recompute plan completion as delivered engagements over approved engagements and compare it to the figure reported to the committee.
Treat a material activity never audited within the stated cycle as an exception.
testing.done: the audit universe covers every material activity, the governance functions are covered within the cycle, and reported completion recomputes.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of engagements, findings and closures
actions: Take 100 percent of engagements rated high risk and 100 percent of findings rated critical or high.
Take 10 closed findings and 8 engagements by seeded random selection from the remainder.
Record the seed, the strata, the population sizes and the selection date for redrawing.
Ensure the sample includes at least one engagement over each of the four key functions.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all high-risk engagements and critical findings, and touches each key function.

testing.step: Re-perform the closure evidence on sampled findings
actions: Open each sampled closed finding and read the closure evidence attached, not the closure comment.
Independently re-test one instance of the remediated control - pull a transaction, open the system configuration screen, read the approved procedure version.
Confirm the closure was validated by someone other than the action owner.
Reopen and log as an exception any finding whose evidence is a status email, a screenshot of a task board, or nothing at all.
testing.done: each sampled closure is supported by re-tested evidence validated by someone other than the action owner.

testing.step: Test internal audit independence in practice
actions: Cross-reference each sampled engagement's team against the HR record of prior roles to detect anyone auditing a process they operated inside the charter's cooling-off period.
Confirm the Chief Audit Executive's reporting line, objective setting and remuneration are set by the Audit Committee, not by executive management.
Read the committee minutes for any recorded scope restriction, delayed access or challenge to a finding, and confirm each was escalated and resolved.
Confirm current independence attestations exist for every auditor on the sampled engagements.
testing.done: no sampled engagement shows a self-review breach, the CAE reporting line is committee-set, and attestations are current.

testing.step: Re-perform the external audit timetable and dating checks
actions: Compare the audit report signature date to the SFCR disclosure date and confirm the opinion pre-dates the publication of the audited elements.
Compare the management representation letter date to the audit report date and confirm it is not earlier.
Recompute the registry filing deadline from the financial year end under the local companies act and compare it to the actual filing receipt date.
Treat any opinion signed after disclosure, or any filing after the statutory deadline, as a fail.
testing.done: opinion, representation letter and registry filing dates all recompute correctly against disclosure and statutory deadlines.

testing.step: Test the adjustment log and the unadjusted difference position
actions: Trace each accepted audit adjustment to a posted journal in the general ledger with the correct period and account.
Confirm each adjustment affecting Solvency II values was pushed through the valuation bridge and not only into the IFRS accounts.
Recompute the aggregate of unadjusted differences and compare it to performance materiality on both the IFRS and the Solvency II bases.
Confirm management's written rationale exists for every declined adjustment above the trivial threshold.
testing.done: every accepted adjustment is posted on both bases and the unadjusted aggregate recomputes below performance materiality with written rationales.

testing.step: Test auditor independence and non-audit service governance
actions: Extract all purchase orders and invoices paid to the audit firm and its network in the year from the procurement system.
Classify each engagement as audit, audit-related or non-audit and compare the non-audit fee total to the audit fee cap applying to public-interest entities.
Confirm each non-audit service was pre-approved by the Audit Committee before it was engaged, using the minute date against the purchase order date.
Flag any prohibited service category and any service engaged without pre-approval as an exception.
testing.done: the non-audit fee position is recomputed against the cap and every service traces to a pre-dated Audit Committee approval.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the engagement or finding reference, what failed and the governance consequence.
Assign a root cause from the standard set - closure evidence not obtained, self-review not screened, plan slipped without committee approval, opinion dated late, non-audit service not pre-approved.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and escalate independence breaches to the Audit Committee chair directly rather than through management.
Carry every open exception into next year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and, for independence breaches, a direct committee-chair escalation.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the audit coordination test
actions: Compute the finding-closure validation rate and the plan completion rate and compare both to the agreed thresholds.
State the conclusion on whether the internal audit function is effective, objective and independent of operational functions as Art. 47 requires, with the evidence references behind it.
Have the reviewer, who sits outside both finance and internal audit, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Audit Committee and, where the conclusion is ineffective, to the administrative body directly, and file the workpaper.
testing.done: a signed workpaper stating a conclusion on internal audit effectiveness and independence is filed and reported to the Audit Committee.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the single Solvency II regulatory calendar across every EEA entity and branch - periodic supervisory submissions, public disclosures, fit-and-proper notifications and ad hoc supervisory requests - and the evidence that each was delivered on time

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Art. 273 on the written fit-and-proper policy, its assessment procedure, criteria, required evidence and re-assessment triggers, read with Directive 2009/138/EC Art. 42 on notifying the supervisory authority of appointments and changes to key function holders and Art. 35 on the periodic reporting deadlines

In-scope processes.value: Regulatory calendar maintenance - obligation registration, deadline derivation, owner assignment, reminder configuration, timeliness evidence capture and late-filing escalation - covering periodic reporting, SFCR disclosure, ORSA supervisory reporting and Art. 42 fit-and-proper notifications for every entity and branch

In-scope systems.value: Obligation register holding one row per entity per obligation per period, with the derived due date, the owner, the reminder rule, the submission identifier and the on-time flag

Compliance procedure documented.value: Regulatory Calendar Procedure - obligation intake from horizon scanning, deadline derivation rules per obligation type and jurisdiction, owner and deputy assignment, reminder cadence, evidence-of-timeliness standard and the late-filing escalation path

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and reviewed at least annually; re-opened whenever a national competent authority issues a reporting circular, EIOPA changes a submission deadline, or a new entity or branch is added to the group

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: All of them, by design - 5 and 11 week quarterly windows, 14 and 20 week annual windows, SFCR publication at 14 and 20 weeks, the ORSA supervisory report within 2 weeks of the assessment being completed, and Art. 42 notifications of key function holder appointments and dismissals within the period the NCA specifies

Deadline reminders configured.value: Automatic reminders to the owner and deputy at due date minus 30, 15, 7, 3 and 1 working days, plus a daily overdue alert to the Head of Compliance from the day after the due date until the row is closed

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: For every calendar row - the derived due date with its rule, the submission identifier or acknowledgement, the timestamp, the on-time flag and the approver - retained 10 years and reportable as a single timeliness register

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every late, missed, rejected or unregistered obligation is logged with the entity, the days late, the cause and whether the national competent authority was notified before or after the deadline passed

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The Head of Compliance signs off every missed deadline, every retrospective calendar addition, and confirms the corrective change to the calendar rule that prevents the recurrence

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every calendar row with a due date in the period across all entities and branches, plus the independently rebuilt expected-obligation list derived from the legal-entity register, the licence schedule and the key function holder register

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Target 100 percent on-time; any obligation delivered after its due date without a pre-agreed extension is a fail, and any obligation that existed in law but had no calendar row is a severe fail regardless of whether it was delivered

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is continuous, so completeness and timeliness are tested monthly on the rows that fell due that month, with a full-year completeness rebuild each January against the legal-entity and licence registers

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not own or maintain any calendar row and must not be the submitter for any tested obligation

Evidence location for test results.value: Monthly regulatory calendar test workpaper - obligation rebuild, row-to-acknowledgement match, due-date recomputation and exception log - filed in the compliance evidence repository by month

Regulator-ready documentation.value: A timeliness register export by entity showing obligation, statutory basis, due date, delivery date, days early or late and the acknowledgement identifier, producible within 3 working days of a supervisory request

Regulator response path.value: The Head of Compliance owns supervisory correspondence about late or missed filings; the entity notifies the NCA in advance whenever a deadline will be missed and requests any extension in writing before the due date, never after

checklist.step: Rebuild the obligation inventory from the legal-entity and licence registers
actions: Extract every EEA insurance and reinsurance undertaking, branch and freedom-of-services registration from the legal-entity register, with its home supervisor and its licence classes.
For each entity derive the obligations that follow from its status - quarterly and annual templates, RSR, SFCR, ORSA supervisory report, Art. 42 notifications, national add-on returns.
Add the group-level obligations where the entity is the ultimate or intermediate parent - group templates, group SFCR, group ORSA, intra-group transaction and risk concentration reporting.
Compare the derived list to the existing calendar and open a row for every obligation not already registered.
Record the statutory basis - the article or the NCA circular reference - on every row so a reader can verify why it exists.
checklist.done: every entity and branch has a derived obligation set registered on the calendar, each row carrying its statutory basis.

checklist.step: Derive the due date for each obligation from a written rule
actions: Set the deadline rule per obligation type - solo quarterly at reference date plus 5 weeks, group quarterly plus 11 weeks, solo annual plus 14 weeks, group annual plus 20 weeks, ORSA supervisory report at completion date plus 2 weeks.
Encode the working-day treatment the NCA applies, including national public holidays for each jurisdiction, rather than assuming calendar days.
Where a national add-on return has its own deadline, record it separately with the circular reference instead of inheriting the harmonised rule.
Set an internal target date ahead of the regulatory due date - 5 working days for periodic returns - so the calendar drives early delivery.
Store the rule alongside the derived date so any date can be recomputed and challenged.
checklist.done: every calendar row shows a derived regulatory due date, the rule that produced it, the working-day treatment and an earlier internal target date.

checklist.step: Assign a named owner and a deputy to every calendar row
actions: Assign a named individual owner - never a team mailbox - and a named deputy to each row.
Confirm each owner has the portal entitlement needed to actually deliver the obligation, and raise the access request now if not.
Run a joiners-movers-leavers sweep monthly against the HR feed and reassign any row whose owner has left or changed role.
Publish the ownership map to the Chief Financial Officer and the Chief Risk Officer each quarter.
checklist.done: every row has a named owner and deputy with the entitlements to deliver it, refreshed against the HR feed monthly.

checklist.step: Register the fit-and-proper notification obligations against the key function register
actions: Extract the current holders of the four key functions - risk management, compliance, internal audit, actuarial - and every member of the administrative, management or supervisory body, per entity.
For each, record the date of the last fitness and propriety assessment and the re-assessment trigger set in the written policy under Delegated Regulation Art. 273.
Create a calendar row for each Art. 42 notification obligation - appointment, resignation, dismissal or change of responsibility - with the NCA's stated notification period.
Create recurring rows for periodic re-assessment - annual self-declaration and refreshed criminal record and regulatory-reference checks at the policy's stated interval.
Link each row to the person record so a departure automatically raises the notification obligation.
checklist.done: every key function holder and board member has registered assessment and notification rows linked to their person record.

checklist.step: Configure the reminder and escalation cadence
actions: Set reminders on each row at due date minus 30, 15, 7, 3 and 1 working days to the owner and the deputy.
Set a daily overdue notification to the Head of Compliance for any row still open past its due date.
Set an escalation at internal target date to the functional head where the row has no evidence attached.
Test the reminder configuration by advancing a test row and confirming the notifications actually fire to the right recipients.
Re-test the configuration after any platform upgrade - silent reminder failure is the most common cause of a missed deadline.
checklist.done: reminders and overdue escalations are configured on every row and proven to fire by a test row.

checklist.step: Capture proof of delivery on every closed row
actions: Require, for each closed row, the portal acknowledgement or the NCA receipt carrying the submission identifier and the server timestamp.
Reject internal status emails, screenshots of an upload screen and self-declared completion as evidence of timeliness.
Compute days early or late as delivery timestamp minus regulatory due date and write it on the row.
Link the evidence file to the row so the register export carries a working link, not a file name.
checklist.done: every closed row holds an NCA acknowledgement with an identifier and timestamp, plus a computed days-early figure.

checklist.step: Register the ad hoc and event-driven supervisory obligations
actions: Open a row whenever an event triggers a supervisory obligation - a major development affecting solvency, a breach of the SCR or MCR, an ORSA performed outside the annual cycle, a change of qualifying holding.

For an SCR breach, register the immediate notification and the realistic recovery plan due within 2 months of observing the breach; for an MCR breach, the short-term finance scheme due within 1 month.
For an ad hoc supervisory request, register the response date the NCA stated in its letter and attach the letter to the row.
Assign an owner the same day the event is identified rather than waiting for the next calendar review.
checklist.done: every event-driven obligation has a same-day row with its statutory response window and the triggering letter or event record attached.

checklist.step: Operate horizon scanning so new obligations reach the calendar before they bite
actions: Monitor the Official Journal, EIOPA publications and each home and host NCA's circular page on a fixed weekly cadence.
Log each change with its effective date, the entities it touches and whether it creates, amends or removes an obligation.
Convert every change that creates or amends an obligation into a calendar row or a rule change within 10 working days of publication.
Report the horizon-scanning log to the Risk Committee quarterly with the calendar changes it produced.
checklist.done: the horizon-scanning log shows a weekly scan and every obligation-creating change converted into a calendar row within 10 working days.

checklist.step: Apply change control to the calendar itself
actions: Restrict the ability to change a due date, delete a row or close a row without evidence to a named administrator group.
Require a reason code and an approver on any due-date change and retain the prior value in the audit trail.
Run a monthly report of all date changes, deletions and evidence-free closures and review each with the Head of Compliance.
Block back-dating of closure timestamps so the on-time flag cannot be manufactured.
checklist.done: date changes, deletions and evidence-free closures are restricted, reason-coded, retained in an audit trail and reviewed monthly.

checklist.step: Run the weekly calendar stand-up on the forward 30-day window
actions: Circulate the rows due in the next 30 days grouped by entity and owner ahead of the stand-up.
Walk each row: is the data available, is the preparer resourced, is the approver diarised, is the portal access valid.
Mark any row at risk with a reason and an agreed recovery action with a date.
Minute the at-risk list and send it to the functional heads the same day.
checklist.done: every row due in the next 30 days has been walked, with at-risk rows carrying a reason, a recovery action and a same-day notification to functional heads.

checklist.step: Escalate at-risk and missed deadlines on a fixed path
actions: At due date minus 3 working days, escalate any row without evidence to the accountable executive with the specific blocker named.
Where a deadline will be missed, notify the NCA supervisory contact in writing before the due date with the reason and the committed delivery date.
Raise a tracker issue for every missed deadline with days late, cause, entity and whether the NCA was told in advance.
Take every missed statutory deadline to the Risk Committee and, where it is material, to the administrative body.
checklist.done: every at-risk row is escalated at due date minus 3 days and every miss is pre-notified to the NCA and reported to the Risk Committee.

checklist.step: Publish the monthly timeliness dashboard
actions: Compute on-time percentage by entity, by obligation type and by owner for the rows that fell due in the month.
Show open overdue rows with days overdue and the accountable executive named, not the team.
Show calendar completeness - rows added retrospectively during the month, which indicates an intake gap rather than a delivery gap.
Distribute to the CFO, CRO, Head of Compliance and the functional heads within 5 working days of month end.
checklist.done: a monthly dashboard showing on-time percentage, overdue rows and retrospective additions is distributed within 5 working days of month end.

checklist.step: Reconcile the calendar to submissions actually made
actions: Extract every acknowledgement received from each NCA portal in the month independently of the calendar.
Match each acknowledgement to a calendar row and investigate any acknowledgement with no row - that is an obligation the calendar did not know about.
Investigate any closed row whose acknowledgement cannot be found in the portal extract.
Record both directions of break on the monthly completeness report.
checklist.done: portal acknowledgements and calendar rows are reconciled in both directions with every break investigated and recorded.

checklist.step: Perform the annual calendar attestation
actions: Have each entity's accountable executive attest in writing that the calendar rows for their entity are complete and correctly owned.
Have the Regulatory Reporting Manager attest that every due date derives from a documented rule and that no rule was changed without approval.
Present the annual timeliness statistics and the attestations to the Risk Committee.
Record any qualification an attestor makes and open a remediation row for it.
checklist.done: written attestations on completeness, ownership and date-rule integrity exist for every entity and are tabled at the Risk Committee.

checklist.step: Archive the timeliness register and the evidence links
actions: Export the timeliness register at each month end - entity, obligation, statutory basis, due date, delivery timestamp, days early or late, acknowledgement identifier.
Archive the export together with the acknowledgement files so the register can be reconstructed without the live platform.
Apply the 10-year retention label and index by entity, obligation type and period.
Confirm a supervisory request for the timeliness register can be met from the archive within 3 working days.
checklist.done: a month-end timeliness register with linked acknowledgements is archived under a 10-year label and retrievable within 3 working days.

testing.step: Rebuild the expected obligation population independently
actions: Pull the legal-entity register, the licence schedule and the key function holder register directly from their owning systems, not from the calendar.
Derive the obligations each entity, branch and key function holder generates for the tested period from the statutory rules.
Compare the derived list to the calendar rows and list every obligation with no row and every row with no derived basis.
Sign the reconciled population as complete with the extraction date and source versions.
testing.done: the independently derived obligation list is reconciled to the calendar with every unmatched item listed, and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile calendar rows to portal acknowledgements in both directions
actions: Extract every acknowledgement received from each NCA portal in the period.
Match acknowledgements to calendar rows and list acknowledgements with no row, which prove the calendar was incomplete.
List closed rows with no matching acknowledgement, which prove the on-time flag was set without evidence.
Treat both break types as exceptions without judgement applied.
testing.done: every acknowledgement matches a row and every closed row matches an acknowledgement, or the break is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of calendar rows
actions: Take 100 percent of rows closed after their due date, 100 percent of rows added retrospectively and 100 percent of Art. 42 fit-and-proper notification rows.
Take 25 further rows by seeded random selection across entities and obligation types.
Record the seed, the strata, the population size and the selection date so the sample can be redrawn.
Ensure the sample covers every jurisdiction the group reports into.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all late, retrospective and fit-and-proper rows, and spans every reporting jurisdiction.

testing.step: Recompute the due date on each sampled row from the underlying rule
actions: Read the statutory basis cited on the row and recompute the due date from the reference date without looking at the stored date.
Apply the jurisdiction's working-day and public-holiday treatment as the NCA states it.
Compare the recomputed date to the stored date and treat any difference as an exception, including a stored date that is later than the statutory one.
Capture the source text or circular page relied on into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled due date is independently recomputed from its cited statutory basis with the source text captured.

testing.step: Re-perform the timeliness computation on the sample
actions: Take the acknowledgement timestamp from the portal evidence, not from the calendar field, for each sampled row.
Recompute days early or late against the recomputed due date and compare to the stored on-time flag.
Investigate any row where a stored on-time flag disagrees with the recomputation, and check the audit trail for a back-dated closure.
List every genuinely late delivery with its days late and whether an advance written extension existed.
testing.done: timeliness is recomputed from portal timestamps on every sampled row and every disagreement with the stored flag is investigated.

testing.step: Test the fit-and-proper notification rows against actual personnel events
actions: Extract every appointment, departure and role change affecting a key function holder or board member in the period from the HR system.
Match each event to an Art. 42 notification row and confirm the notification to the NCA was made inside the stated period.

Confirm each appointment has a completed fitness and propriety assessment predating the appointment, with the evidence the written policy requires under Art. 273 - qualifications, experience, criminal record check, regulatory references.
List any personnel event with no notification row as a severe exception.
testing.done: every key-function personnel event matches a timely NCA notification and a pre-dated fit-and-proper assessment.

testing.step: Test the reminder configuration and the change-control trail
actions: Confirm each sampled row carries the full reminder ladder at minus 30, 15, 7, 3 and 1 working days to a named owner and deputy.
Pull the notification delivery log and confirm the reminders actually sent, rather than only being configured.
Extract every due-date change, row deletion and evidence-free closure in the period and confirm each has a reason code and an approver.
Treat any due-date change that moved a date later without an approver, or any back-dated closure timestamp, as a severe exception.
testing.done: reminders are proven to have sent and every date change, deletion and evidence-free closure carries a reason code and an approver.

testing.step: Test owner validity against the HR and entitlement feeds
actions: Cross-reference every sampled row owner and deputy against the HR active-employee feed at the row's due date.
Confirm each owner held the portal entitlement required to deliver the obligation at that date.
List rows owned by leavers, by a team mailbox, or by someone without the delivery entitlement.
Confirm the monthly joiners-movers-leavers sweep ran in every month of the period.
testing.done: every sampled row had a live, entitled, named owner at its due date and the monthly ownership sweep is evidenced for each month.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the entity, the obligation, the days late or the missing row and the supervisory consequence.
Assign a root cause from the standard set - obligation never registered, due-date rule wrong, reminder never fired, owner left, evidence not captured, closure back-dated.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and for any missed statutory deadline confirm whether the NCA was notified in advance.
Carry every open exception into the next month's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a recorded NCA notification position.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the calendar test
actions: Compute the on-time rate and the calendar completeness rate and compare both to the 100 percent target.
State the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - with the workpaper references behind it.
Have the reviewer, who owns no calendar row and submitted no tested obligation, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and every missed statutory deadline to the Risk Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper stating on-time rate, completeness rate and a conclusion is filed and reported to the Risk Committee.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the contingency plan set that evidences continuity and regularity in the performance of activities, from the business impact analysis through to the administrative body's annual approval

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Directive 2009/138/EC Art. 41(4) requiring reasonable steps to ensure continuity and regularity including contingency plans, read with Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Art. 258(1)(f)-(g) on appropriate and proportionate systems, resources and procedures and on business continuity and emergency plans, and Art. 45(1)(a) linking overall solvency needs to the risk profile in the ORSA

In-scope processes.value: Business continuity lifecycle - identification of critical business functions, business impact analysis, recovery objective setting, contingency and crisis plan authoring, third-party dependency continuity and annual administrative body approval - across underwriting, claims, policy administration, investment, finance and supervisory reporting

In-scope systems.value: Continuity module holding the critical function inventory, business impact analyses, recovery time and point objectives, plan documents, dependency maps and the approval and review dates

Compliance procedure documented.value: Business Continuity Policy and Plan Standard - criticality criteria, the BIA method and impact scales, RTO and RPO setting rules, plan content template, crisis management structure and activation thresholds, third-party continuity requirements and the annual review trigger set

Compliance procedure approved.value: Policy approved by the administrative, management or supervisory body annually as part of the system of governance policy set; individual plans approved by their function head and noted by the Operational Risk Committee

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual policy and plan review with board approval before the year-end governance cycle closes; plan re-review within 30 days of any material change - a system migration, an outsourcing of a critical function, a site move or a reorganisation - and continuity outcomes fed into the annual ORSA

Deadline reminders configured.value: Plan review tasks fire 60 and 30 days before each plan's anniversary date, plus an event-driven task raised automatically when a change record touches a system supporting a critical function

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Signed BIAs, approved plans with version history, dependency maps, crisis structure and call trees, board approval minutes and the ORSA continuity input retained 10 years in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Critical functions with no current BIA, plans past their review date, RTOs the technical recovery capability cannot meet and critical outsourcers without a continuity clause are each logged with owner and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The CRO signs off any accepted gap between a business-stated RTO and the achievable technical recovery time, and any critical function operating without an approved plan

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every business function on the critical function inventory, with its BIA, its stated RTO and RPO, its contingency plan and its supporting application, site and third-party dependencies

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100 percent of critical functions must hold a BIA and an approved plan reviewed within the last 12 months; any RTO not supported by a demonstrated technical recovery capability is a fail; any critical outsourced function with no continuity and exit provision in contract is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is an annual review with event-driven refresh, so plan currency and coverage are tested annually ahead of board approval and re-tested within 30 days of any material change event

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer sits in the risk management function, outside the continuity team that authored the plans and outside the business functions being assessed

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual continuity assurance workpaper - inventory reconciliation, BIA and plan currency test, RTO feasibility comparison and third-party clause test - filed in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Critical function inventory with BIAs, approved plans, RTO and RPO register, dependency map and the board approval minute, producible to the national competent authority within 10 working days of a governance review request

Regulator response path.value: The Chief Risk Officer answers NCA questions on continuity arrangements as part of the system of governance review; a continuity failure affecting policyholders is escalated to the NCA under the Art. 35(2) major-development route

checklist.step: Refresh the critical business function inventory
actions: Take the process inventory and score each function against the criticality criteria - policyholder harm, regulatory breach, financial loss, reputational impact - on the published scales.

Confirm the functions that discharge a legal duty are always in scope: claims payment, policyholder servicing, premium collection, supervisory reporting, investment settlement and technical provisions calculation.
Have each function head confirm or challenge the criticality rating in writing and record the outcome.
Publish the approved inventory with an owner per function and a version date.
checklist.done: the critical function inventory is scored, confirmed in writing by each function head, and published with owners and a version date.

checklist.step: Run the business impact analysis for each critical function
actions: Interview the function owner and record the impact of outage at 4 hours, 24 hours, 3 days and 1 week across the four impact dimensions.
Record the peak periods when an outage would hurt most - month-end close, quarterly reporting weeks, catastrophe response, renewal season.
Record the minimum resource level needed to run the function in degraded mode: headcount, skills, applications, data, workspace.
Identify the maximum tolerable period of disruption and have the function owner sign the BIA.
Store the signed BIA against the function record with its assessment date.
checklist.done: each critical function holds a signed, dated BIA stating time-based impacts, peak periods, minimum resources and the maximum tolerable disruption.

checklist.step: Set and validate recovery time and recovery point objectives
actions: Derive a proposed RTO for each function from its maximum tolerable period of disruption, leaving a margin rather than setting them equal.
Derive the RPO from the data loss the function can absorb - for premium and claims payment ledgers this is usually near zero.
Send each proposed RTO and RPO to IT Operations for a written statement of the achievable recovery time and data loss on the current architecture.
Where the achievable figure is worse than the business requirement, record the gap, its consequence and either a remediation project or a CRO-signed acceptance.
Publish the agreed RTO and RPO register and link each entry to its supporting applications.
checklist.done: every critical function has an agreed RTO and RPO, a written IT feasibility statement, and either a remediation plan or a signed acceptance for any gap.

checklist.step: Map the dependencies behind each critical function
actions: Map each critical function to its supporting applications in the configuration database, including upstream data feeds and downstream consumers.
Map the infrastructure beneath those applications - data centre or cloud region, database, network path, authentication service.
Map the people dependencies - the roles that must be available, the minimum headcount and any single points of knowledge.
Map the third-party dependencies - outsourced services, cloud providers, brokers, claims handlers, payment processors - and flag those supporting a critical or important function.
Flag every single point of failure surfaced by the map and raise it as a risk with an owner.
checklist.done: each critical function has a dependency map covering applications, infrastructure, people and third parties, with single points of failure raised as owned risks.

checklist.step: Author or refresh the contingency plan for each critical function
actions: Write the plan to the standard template: activation criteria, roles and deputies, first-hour actions, degraded-mode operating procedure, manual workaround, recovery sequence and return-to-normal criteria.
State explicitly how the function is delivered while the primary system is unavailable - the manual workaround must be executable by staff who have not done it before.
Include the contact tree with deputies, out-of-hours numbers and the third-party escalation contacts from the contracts.
Include the customer and regulator communication steps and who is authorised to send them.
Have the function head approve the plan and record the approval date and version.
checklist.done: each critical function holds an approved, versioned plan with activation criteria, an executable manual workaround and a current contact tree.

checklist.step: Define the crisis management structure and activation thresholds
actions: Define the crisis team membership - chair, operations, IT, communications, legal, HR, risk - with a named deputy for every seat.
Set the activation thresholds that move an incident from major-incident management to crisis management, in measurable terms rather than judgement alone.
Define the decision rights the crisis team holds: invoking failover, standing down a site, authorising emergency spend, approving external statements.
Set the battle rhythm - situation report cadence, log keeping, decision recording - so the response is reconstructable afterwards.
Publish the structure and confirm every named member and deputy has acknowledged their role.
checklist.done: a crisis structure with named members and deputies, measurable activation thresholds and defined decision rights is published and acknowledged.

checklist.step: Push continuity requirements into critical third-party arrangements
actions: List every third party the dependency map flags as supporting a critical or important function.

Check each contract for the continuity provisions - service continuity obligation, RTO and RPO commitments, testing rights, incident notification timelines, audit and access rights, and an exit and transition plan.
Obtain the provider's own continuity and disaster recovery plan and its most recent test results, and assess them against the function's RTO.
Raise a contract amendment where a provision is missing and track it to signature.
Record substitutability and the identified alternative provider or in-house fallback for each critical dependency.
checklist.done: every critical third party has assessed continuity provisions, provider test evidence and a recorded substitutability position.

checklist.step: Build the severe but plausible scenario set the plans must withstand
actions: Define scenarios covering loss of a primary data centre or cloud region, loss of a major office, loss of a critical third party, a destructive cyber attack with data corruption, and extended loss of key staff.
For each scenario name the critical functions affected, the dependencies removed and the assumed duration.
Have the Chief Risk Officer confirm each scenario is severe but plausible for this undertaking's risk profile rather than generic.
Map each scenario to the plans that would be invoked, so a plan with no scenario is questioned and a scenario with no plan is a gap.
Publish the scenario set as the input to the annual test programme.
checklist.done: a CRO-confirmed severe but plausible scenario set exists, mapped to the plans it invokes, with gaps in either direction raised.

checklist.step: Feed continuity risk into the ORSA
actions: Take the residual operational risk arising from the continuity gaps and unremediated single points of failure into the ORSA operational risk assessment.
Quantify the financial impact of the most severe plausible scenario on own funds and on the solvency position over the business planning horizon.
Confirm the ORSA narrative describes the continuity arrangements and states how they support the overall solvency needs assessment under Art. 45(1)(a).
Record the ORSA conclusions that require a continuity improvement as owned actions on the continuity plan of work.
checklist.done: continuity residual risk is quantified in the ORSA, described in its narrative, and ORSA-driven improvements are owned actions.

checklist.step: Train the responders and prove they can find and use the plan
actions: Assign role-based continuity training to every named plan role, crisis team member and deputy, with a completion deadline.
Run a plan familiarisation walkthrough per critical function at least annually and record attendance.
Confirm each responder can retrieve the plan when the primary systems are down - offline copies, printed crisis packs, out-of-band contact lists.
Track completion in the learning platform and escalate non-completion to the function head.
checklist.done: every named responder has completed role-based training, attended a walkthrough and demonstrated offline access to the plan.

checklist.step: Operate event-driven plan review as well as the annual cycle
actions: Configure the change process so any change record touching an application mapped to a critical function raises a continuity review task.
Add the same trigger for a new or terminated critical outsourcing, a site move, a reorganisation of a critical function and a material incident.
Complete the triggered review within 30 days, updating the BIA, the dependency map and the plan as needed.
Record the trigger, the review date and the change made on the plan version history.
checklist.done: material change events automatically raise a continuity review that is completed within 30 days and recorded in the plan version history.

checklist.step: Review continuity status at the Operational Risk Committee
actions: Table a quarterly pack showing plan currency by function, open RTO gaps, unremediated single points of failure and third-party continuity exceptions.
Challenge any function whose plan has been rolled forward with no substantive change for two cycles.
Record committee decisions on accepting or remediating each gap with an owner and a date.
Escalate to the Risk Committee any critical function operating without an approved plan.
checklist.done: the Operational Risk Committee has a quarterly record of plan currency, gaps and decisions with owners and dates.

checklist.step: Obtain administrative body approval of the policy and the plan set
actions: Submit the business continuity policy, the critical function inventory, the RTO and RPO register and the summary of open gaps to the administrative body.
Table the approval resolution as part of the annual system of governance policy review required by Delegated Regulation Art. 258.
Minute the body's challenge on the accepted gaps and its decision on each.
Record the approval date, which sets the next annual review anniversary for every plan.
checklist.done: a dated board approval of the continuity policy and plan set exists, with accepted gaps individually minuted.

checklist.step: Distribute the approved plans under version control
actions: Publish the approved version of every plan to the repository and retire the prior version so two versions cannot circulate.
Distribute the offline crisis pack - plan extract, contact tree, activation criteria - to every named responder and record acknowledgement.
Confirm the offline copies are refreshed whenever a plan version changes, since a stale contact tree is the most common failure in a live event.
Record the distribution list and acknowledgements against the plan version.
checklist.done: only the approved version of each plan is live, offline crisis packs are distributed, and acknowledgements are recorded against the version.

checklist.step: Archive the continuity evidence set
actions: Archive the inventory, signed BIAs, RTO and RPO register with the IT feasibility statements, plans with version history, dependency maps and third-party assessments.
Archive the board approval minute and the Operational Risk Committee packs that evidence ongoing oversight.
Apply the 10-year retention label and index by function, plan version and approval date.
Confirm a supervisory request for the continuity arrangements can be met from the archive within 10 working days.
checklist.done: the full continuity evidence set is archived under a 10-year label, indexed by function and version, and retrievable within 10 working days.

testing.step: Build the population of critical functions and their plans
actions: Extract the critical function inventory with, for each function, the BIA date, the RTO, the RPO, the plan version and the plan approval date.

Rebuild the expected critical function list independently from the process inventory and the legal-duty list - claims payment, policyholder servicing, premium collection, supervisory reporting, investment settlement, technical provisions calculation.
Compare the two lists and treat any legally required function missing from the inventory as a severe exception.
Sign the reconciled population as complete with the extraction date.
testing.done: the inventory is reconciled to an independently rebuilt critical function list with every omission raised, and signed as complete.

testing.step: Test BIA and plan currency across the whole population
actions: For every critical function, compute the age of the BIA and of the plan approval against the test date.
List every function whose BIA or plan is older than 12 months, and every function with no plan at all.
Cross-check against the change and outsourcing records for the period to find plans that should have had an event-driven review and did not.
Compute the coverage percentage against the 100 percent requirement.
testing.done: BIA and plan currency is computed for every critical function with the coverage percentage stated and every stale or missing plan listed.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of functions for deep testing
actions: Take 100 percent of functions with the shortest RTOs and 100 percent of functions materially dependent on a critical outsourcer.
Take 8 further functions by seeded random selection from the remainder.
Record the seed, the strata, the population size and the selection date so the sample can be redrawn.
Ensure the sample spans underwriting, claims, finance and supervisory reporting.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all shortest-RTO and outsourcer-dependent functions, and spans the main business areas.

testing.step: Re-perform the RTO feasibility comparison against technical capability
actions: For each sampled function, list the supporting applications from the configuration database and pull each application's documented recovery tier and last demonstrated recovery time.
Compare the slowest supporting application's demonstrated recovery time to the function's stated RTO.
Compare the backup and replication frequency to the stated RPO - a nightly backup cannot support a one-hour RPO.
List every function whose RTO or RPO is not supported by demonstrated capability, and check whether a CRO-signed acceptance exists.
testing.done: each sampled RTO and RPO is compared to demonstrated technical capability with every unsupported objective listed and its acceptance status checked.

testing.step: Test the dependency maps against the live configuration
actions: For each sampled function, walk the dependency map with the function owner and an infrastructure engineer.
Compare the mapped applications to the actual applications used, including shadow tools and spreadsheets the map omits.
Confirm the mapped infrastructure matches the current hosting arrangement, particularly after any cloud migration during the year.
List every unmapped dependency, since a dependency that is not mapped will not be recovered.
testing.done: each sampled dependency map is walked against live usage and configuration with every unmapped dependency listed.

testing.step: Test the plan content against the standard and its executability
actions: Score each sampled plan against the template - activation criteria, roles and deputies, first-hour actions, degraded-mode procedure, manual workaround, recovery sequence, return-to-normal criteria.
Read the manual workaround and judge whether a trained but inexperienced person could execute it from the text alone.
Sample 10 contacts from each plan's contact tree and verify each against the HR feed and the third-party contract for currency.
Treat a plan whose workaround is a single sentence, or whose contact tree contains leavers, as a fail.
testing.done: each sampled plan is scored against the template, its workaround judged executable, and its contact tree verified against HR and contract records.

testing.step: Test the continuity provisions in critical third-party contracts
actions: Pull the executed contract for each critical third party in the sample and locate the continuity, testing rights, incident notification, audit rights and exit clauses.
Compare the provider's committed recovery time to the function's RTO and list any contract that commits to less than the business needs.
Confirm the provider's most recent continuity test evidence is on file and dated within the last 12 months.
List any critical dependency with no continuity clause, no test evidence or no recorded alternative provider.
testing.done: each sampled critical contract is checked for continuity, testing, notification, audit and exit provisions with current provider test evidence on file.

testing.step: Test governance, approval and training evidence
actions: Confirm the administrative body approved the continuity policy and the plan set within the last 12 months and that the minute records challenge on accepted gaps.
Confirm the Operational Risk Committee received the quarterly continuity pack in every quarter of the period.
Pull training completion for every named plan role and crisis team seat in the sample and compute the completion rate.
Confirm every crisis team seat has a named, acknowledged deputy.
testing.done: board approval, quarterly committee oversight, training completion and deputy coverage are each evidenced for the period.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the function, the plan version, the gap and the impact on the maximum tolerable period of disruption.

Assign a root cause from the standard set - function not on inventory, BIA not refreshed, RTO not validated with IT, dependency unmapped, contract clause missing, training not completed, event-driven review skipped.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and escalate any critical function with no approved plan to the Chief Risk Officer immediately.
Carry every open exception into next year's assurance as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and, where a plan is absent, an immediate CRO escalation.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the continuity assurance
actions: Compute plan coverage, plan currency and RTO feasibility rates and compare each to the 100 percent requirement.
State the conclusion on whether the undertaking has taken reasonable steps to ensure continuity and regularity in the performance of its activities, with workpaper references.
Have the reviewer, who authored no plan and owns no sampled function, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Risk Committee before the administrative body approves the policy set, and file the workpaper.
testing.done: a signed workpaper stating coverage, currency and feasibility rates with a conclusion is filed and reported before board approval.
