Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside IT operations and must not have executed, validated or reported any sampled test

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual resilience testing assurance workpaper - test coverage reconciliation, RTO and RPO re-measurement, integrity result review and findings ageing - filed in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Test calendar with coverage status, per-test reports showing scenario, measured RTO and RPO, integrity results and sign-offs, plus the internal model recovery evidence, producible to the national competent authority within 10 working days

Regulator response path.value: The Chief Information Officer answers NCA questions on recovery capability; where a recovery failure would affect the integrity of reported SCR figures, the Chief Risk Officer notifies the NCA through the supervisory contact before the next submission

checklist.step: Build the annual test programme from the critical function dependency maps
actions: Extract every application mapped to a critical business function with its recovery tier, target RTO and target RPO.
List each application's last test date and rank by staleness so the longest-untested go first in the calendar.
Add the internal model calculation platform, the actuarial modelling environment and the regulatory reporting engine explicitly - they carry supervisory consequences if unrecoverable.
Book a test window for every tier-one application inside the next 12 months, avoiding the year-end close and the supervisory reporting weeks.
Submit the programme to the Operational Risk Committee for approval before the first window opens.
checklist.done: an approved annual test calendar covers every tier-one application within 12 months, with model and reporting platforms explicitly included.

checklist.step: Select the scenario for each test from the approved catalogue
actions: Pick the scenario from the severe but plausible set - primary data centre loss, cloud region failure, storage array corruption, destructive cyber attack requiring restore from immutable backup, or loss of the identity service.
Rotate the scenario per application year on year so the same easy failover is not repeated annually.
State the assumed unavailable components explicitly, including the ones the team is not allowed to use during the test.
Have the Chief Risk Officer or delegate confirm the scenario is representative of the risk profile rather than convenient.
checklist.done: each booked test names a rotated, CRO-confirmed scenario with the unavailable components explicitly listed.

checklist.step: Write the test plan with measurable entry and exit criteria
actions: Write the plan stating scope, scenario, the recovery runbook steps to be executed, the roles involved and the communications during the window.
Set entry criteria - backup verified, change approved, business validator available, rollback path proven.
Set exit criteria as measurable numbers, not opinions: recovered within the target RTO, data loss within the target RPO, every integrity check passed, application returned to primary.
State the measurement method - the clock starts at declared disaster and stops when the business validator confirms the service is usable, not when the infrastructure reports up.
Raise the change record for the window and obtain CAB approval.
checklist.done: an approved test plan exists with numeric exit criteria, a stated clock-start and clock-stop definition and a CAB-approved change record.

checklist.step: Verify backups and replication before the window opens
actions: Confirm the most recent backup for each in-scope system completed successfully and its restore has been verified, not merely reported as green.
Confirm replication lag to the recovery site is inside the target RPO at the moment the test starts, and record the figure.
Confirm the immutable or air-gapped backup copy exists where the scenario is a destructive cyber attack, since replicated corruption is not a recovery source.
Record the backup identifiers and timestamps that will be used for the restore.
checklist.done: verified backups and a measured replication lag inside the RPO are recorded, with immutable copies confirmed for cyber scenarios.

checklist.step: Execute the failover and log every step against the clock
actions: Declare the disaster at a recorded time and start the clock; do not warm anything up before the declaration.
Execute the runbook steps in order, logging the start and end time of each step and any deviation from the written runbook.
Record every step that required knowledge not in the runbook - this is the most valuable finding a test produces.
Escalate to the test director rather than improvising where a step fails, and record the failure before any workaround.
Stop the clock only when the business validator confirms the service is usable for real work.
checklist.done: a timestamped execution log records every runbook step, every deviation and a clock stopped on business confirmation, not infrastructure status.

checklist.step: Measure the achieved recovery time and data loss
actions: Compute achieved RTO as business-usable time minus disaster declaration time and compare it to the target.
Compute achieved RPO as the gap between the last committed transaction before failure and the last transaction present after recovery, from the transaction log rather than an estimate.
Record the recovered environment's capacity relative to production - a recovery running at 40 percent capacity has not met the objective for a peak period.
Write all three measurements into the test record before the environment is failed back, since the evidence disappears afterwards.
checklist.done: achieved RTO, achieved RPO and recovered capacity are measured from logs and recorded before failback.

checklist.step: Validate data integrity in the recovered environment
actions: Run the standing integrity set - record counts by table, control totals on financial and claims balances, referential integrity checks and checksum comparison against the pre-failure snapshot.
Reconcile the recovered policy count, claim count and outstanding reserve total to the pre-test figures and explain every difference against the measured RPO.
Test that in-flight transactions at the point of failure are either fully applied or fully absent, never half-applied.
Record every integrity check with its result and the evidence, and treat any unexplained difference as a test failure.
checklist.done: the full integrity set has run in the recovered environment with counts, control totals and in-flight transaction states reconciled and evidenced.

checklist.step: Re-run the internal model calculation in the recovered environment
actions: Execute the reference model run in the recovered environment using the same input data set, assumptions and model version as the last production run.
Compare the recovered SCR, technical provisions and key intermediate outputs to the production results cell by cell.
Confirm the model version, parameter files, mapping tables and random seeds all restored intact - a model that runs but produces different numbers is a worse outcome than one that does not run.

Confirm the internal model documentation required by Art. 125 and Delegated Regulation Arts. 243-245 - design, operational details, theory, assumptions and limitations - is itself recoverable and readable in the recovered environment.
Record the comparison and have the Chief Actuary sign whether the recovered environment is fit to produce regulatory figures.
checklist.done: the reference model run reproduces production SCR and technical provisions in the recovered environment, with the model documentation recoverable and the Chief Actuary signing fitness.

checklist.step: Have the business validate the recovered service against real work
actions: Give each business validator a scripted set of real transactions to execute - quote and bind a policy, register and pay a claim, run a premium collection, produce a supervisory reporting extract.
Record pass or fail per transaction with the evidence, rather than accepting a general statement that the system looked fine.
Test the integrations that matter - payment file generation, broker feeds, document production - since these commonly fail in a recovered environment.
Have the validator sign the confirmation that stopped the recovery clock.
checklist.done: each scripted business transaction has a recorded pass or fail with evidence and the validator has signed the usability confirmation.

checklist.step: Fail back and prove the primary environment is clean
actions: Execute the failback runbook and record its duration separately - failback failure is a real production risk that testing frequently ignores.
Reconcile the data created during the test window so nothing is lost or duplicated on return to primary.
Confirm replication is re-established and lag is back inside the RPO before the window is closed.
Close the change record with the actual outcome, including any residual configuration drift left behind.
checklist.done: failback is executed and timed, test-window data is reconciled, replication is restored inside the RPO and the change record is closed with the actual outcome.

checklist.step: Hold the debrief while the detail is still fresh
actions: Run the debrief within 2 working days of the test with everyone who executed a step, including the business validators.
Walk the execution log step by step and capture every deviation, delay, missing instruction and undocumented dependency.
Separate findings into runbook defects, capability gaps, capacity shortfalls and process failures, since each goes to a different owner.
Record the honest verdict on whether the recovery would have held for the full duration assumed in the scenario, not just for the test window.
checklist.done: a debrief held within 2 working days has produced classified findings and a stated verdict on sustained recovery.

checklist.step: Issue the test report within 15 working days
actions: Write the report stating scenario, scope, the measured RTO and RPO against target, integrity results, the model re-run comparison, business validation outcome and the findings list.
State plainly whether the test passed or failed against the exit criteria - a test that missed its RTO is a failed test even if the service came back.
Circulate to the application owner, the business function owner, the Business Continuity Manager, the Chief Risk Officer and Internal Audit.
Attach the execution log and the integrity evidence so the report can be verified independently.
checklist.done: a report with measured results, an explicit pass or fail verdict and attached evidence is issued within 15 working days.

checklist.step: Drive the findings backlog to closure before the next cycle
actions: Raise a problem record per finding with severity, owner and target date, linked to the test record and the configuration item.
Fix the runbook defects immediately and republish the runbook version rather than holding them for a project.
Track capability and capacity gaps as funded work with a named sponsor, and escalate any that will not close before the next annual test.
Report findings ageing by severity at the monthly IT service review.
checklist.done: every finding is a tracked problem record, runbook defects are already republished, and ageing is reported monthly.

checklist.step: Retest the failed elements rather than waiting a year
actions: Book a targeted retest within 90 days for any test that missed its RTO or RPO or failed an integrity check.
Scope the retest to the failed elements plus a regression over the steps that previously passed.
Where the retest fails again, escalate to the Chief Information Officer and the Operational Risk Committee for a capability decision rather than another retest.
Record the retest result against the original test record so the history shows both.
checklist.done: every failed test has a booked and executed retest within 90 days, with repeated failure escalated for a capability decision.

checklist.step: Report the annual programme outcome and archive the evidence
actions: Report to the Operational Risk Committee and the Risk Committee the coverage achieved, pass rate, RTO and RPO performance against target and open findings.
Feed the residual recovery risk into the ORSA operational risk assessment for the year.
Archive per test the plan, change record, execution log, measurements, integrity results, model comparison, validator sign-off and report.
Apply the 10-year retention label and index by application, test date and scenario.
checklist.done: the annual programme outcome is reported to committee and fed into the ORSA, with every test evidence pack archived and indexed.

testing.step: Build the population of applications requiring a resilience test
actions: Extract every application mapped to a critical business function with its recovery tier, target RTO and RPO and last test date.
Rebuild the expected tier-one list independently from the critical function dependency maps rather than accepting the IT tiering.
Compare the two lists and list every application supporting a critical function but not tiered for testing.
Sign the reconciled population as complete with the extraction date and source versions.
testing.done: the testable application population is reconciled to the critical function dependency maps with every gap listed, and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the test calendar to tests actually executed
actions: Extract every change record raised for a DR test window in the period and match it to the approved test calendar.
List calendar entries with no executed change record, which are tests that were booked and quietly dropped.
List executed tests with no calendar entry, which indicates the programme is not the source of truth.
Compute annual coverage as tier-one applications tested over tier-one applications in scope.
testing.done: the calendar and executed change records reconcile in both directions and annual tier-one coverage is computed.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of tests for re-performance review
actions: Take 100 percent of tests on the internal model platform, the regulatory reporting engine and the claims payment path.
Take 100 percent of tests reported as failed or partially successful.
Take 6 further tests by seeded random selection from the remainder.
Record the seed, the strata, the population size and the selection date so the sample can be redrawn.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers all model, reporting, payment and failed tests plus a random remainder.

testing.step: Re-measure the achieved RTO and RPO from the raw evidence
actions: Take the disaster declaration timestamp and the business validator confirmation timestamp from the execution log, not from the report summary.
Recompute achieved RTO and compare it to both the reported figure and the target.
Recompute achieved RPO from the transaction log gap rather than the replication dashboard, and compare to the target.
List every test where the reported figure is better than the recomputed figure - a clock started late is the most common cause.
testing.done: RTO and RPO are independently recomputed from raw logs for each sampled test and reconciled to the reported figures.

testing.step: Re-perform the data integrity validation results
actions: Pull the integrity check output retained for each sampled test and confirm the full standing set ran, not a subset.
Re-run two checks against the retained pre-test and post-recovery snapshots where they were preserved.
Confirm every recorded difference is explained by the measured RPO and not simply annotated as expected.
List any test where an integrity check failed and the test was still reported as passed.
testing.done: the full integrity set is evidenced for each sampled test, two checks are re-run, and any failed-but-passed test is listed.

testing.step: Verify the internal model re-run comparison independently
actions: Pull the production reference run and the recovered-environment run for the model platform test and compare SCR, technical provisions and the key intermediate outputs.
Confirm the model version, parameter files and mapping tables used in the recovered run match the production ones by hash or version identifier.
Confirm the internal model documentation required by Arts. 243-245 was accessible in the recovered environment and covers theory, assumptions and limitations.
Treat any output difference not explained by a documented input difference as a fail, however small.
testing.done: the recovered model run is independently compared to production on outputs and versions, with the model documentation confirmed recoverable.

testing.step: Test the business validation evidence behind each sampled test
actions: Pull the scripted transaction results and confirm each has a recorded pass or fail with supporting evidence rather than a blanket statement.
Confirm the validator was a business user of the function, not an IT engineer signing on the business's behalf.
Confirm the integrations - payment file, broker feed, document production - were exercised and not skipped as out of scope.
List any test whose clock was stopped without a signed business confirmation.
testing.done: each sampled test carries per-transaction business evidence signed by a genuine business validator, with integrations exercised.

testing.step: Test findings closure and retest discipline
actions: Pull every finding raised from the sampled tests and check each has a problem record, a severity, an owner and a target date.
For findings marked closed, request the evidence - the republished runbook version, the configuration change record, the capacity uplift.
Confirm every failed test had a targeted retest booked and executed within 90 days.
List findings carried forward more than one annual cycle and check whether a CIO sign-off exists.
testing.done: every sampled finding has a tracked record with closure evidence, and every failed test has an executed retest within 90 days.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the application, the test date, the measured shortfall and the business function affected.

Assign a root cause from the standard set - application not tiered, test dropped, clock started late, integrity set truncated, model outputs not compared, finding closed without evidence, retest not booked.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and escalate any untested tier-one application supporting claims payment or supervisory reporting to the CIO and CRO immediately.
Carry every open exception into next year's assurance as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and, for untested critical applications, an immediate CIO and CRO escalation.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the resilience testing assurance
actions: Compute tier-one test coverage, the pass rate against exit criteria and the proportion of tests meeting target RTO and RPO.
State the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - with the workpaper references behind it, including a specific statement on the internal model platform's recoverability.
Have the reviewer, who executed, validated or reported no sampled test, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Risk Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper stating coverage, pass rate and a conclusion including internal model recoverability is filed and reported to the Risk Committee.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the register of critical and important outsourcing and ICT third-party arrangements, including the remuneration and incentive terms in those contracts that must not encourage excessive risk-taking

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Art. 275 as amended by Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/1256 on the written remuneration policy and the integration of sustainability risks, read with Directive 2009/138/EC Art. 46(2) and Delegated Regulation Art. 270 on the compliance function's monitoring, Art. 271(3) on internal audit coverage, and Art. 274 on outsourcing arrangements

In-scope processes.value: Third-party lifecycle - contract intake, criticality classification, register population, subcontracting and concentration analysis, exit strategy maintenance, contractual remuneration and incentive review, and supervisory notification of critical outsourcing

In-scope systems.value: Contract repository holding the executed agreements, their criticality flags, the clause library positions and the renewal and exit dates that feed the register

Compliance procedure documented.value: Third-Party and ICT Risk Register Procedure - intake triggers, the criticality and importance test, register field definitions and identifier standards, subcontracting chain capture, concentration thresholds, exit strategy requirements and the annual register attestation

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Risk Officer with the Chief Information Officer countersigning the ICT sections; reviewed annually and re-opened on any change to the outsourcing rules or the register reporting format

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Register maintained continuously with a full reconciliation each quarter; the ICT register of information submitted to the national competent authority annually on the date it specifies; supervisory notification of an intended critical outsourcing made in good time before the arrangement enters into force, and of any subsequent material development in that arrangement

Deadline reminders configured.value: Renewal and exit-review reminders at 180, 90 and 30 days before each critical contract's expiry; a quarterly reconciliation task; and an annual register submission task raised 60 days before the NCA's submission date

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Register versions, criticality assessments, executed contracts with clause mapping, subcontracting disclosures, concentration analyses, exit strategies, supervisory notifications and the annual attestation retained 10 years

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Unregistered critical arrangements, missing provider LEIs, undisclosed subcontractors supporting a critical function, contracts lacking audit or exit rights and critical outsourcings not notified to the NCA are each logged with owner and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The CRO signs off every critical arrangement operating with a missing contractual right, every accepted concentration position and every retrospective supervisory notification

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every live third-party arrangement in the contract repository and every supplier paid in the period per the procurement and accounts payable ledgers, tested against the register entries

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero critical or important arrangements absent from the register; zero critical providers without an LEI and a disclosed subcontracting chain; every critical contract must carry audit, access, incident notification, sub-outsourcing consent and exit provisions - a missing provision is a fail

checklist.step: Sweep every source of third-party arrangements into a single intake
actions: Extract all active supplier records and open purchase orders from the procurement system with spend for the last 12 months.
Extract all executed agreements from the contract repository including framework agreements, statements of work and cloud subscriptions.
Extract accounts payable vendor payments to catch arrangements bought on expense or corporate card outside procurement.
Merge the three sources on legal entity name and tax identifier and de-duplicate, keeping every unmatched record for investigation.
Hand the merged intake list to the Third-Party Risk Manager for classification.
checklist.done: a single de-duplicated intake list built from procurement, contracts and payables exists with every unmatched record retained for investigation.

checklist.step: Classify each arrangement as ICT or non-ICT and test criticality
actions: Tag each arrangement ICT where the service is a digital or data service delivered on an ongoing basis, including cloud, software as a service, hosting, data and network services.

Apply the criticality test: does the arrangement support a critical or important function whose failure would materially impair the undertaking's ability to meet its obligations, comply with its authorisation conditions, or its financial soundness.
Record the specific critical business function supported, taken from the continuity inventory, rather than a generic service description.
Have the function owner countersign the criticality rating, since procurement cannot make that call alone.
Log the classification decision with its date and the evidence relied on.
checklist.done: every arrangement is tagged ICT or non-ICT and criticality-rated against a named critical business function, countersigned by the function owner.

checklist.step: Populate the register entity and contractual arrangement records
actions: Create the entity records: the undertaking's own LEI, its name, country and the entities in scope of the register.
Create one contractual arrangement record per executed contract with the reference, start date, end date, notice period, governing law and annual expense.
Link each arrangement to the entities that make use of it - a group-level cloud contract used by five entities must appear against all five.
Record the currency and the annual cost so concentration and materiality can be computed from the register itself.
Reject any arrangement record with no linked executed contract - a verbal or purchase-order-only critical arrangement is itself a finding.
checklist.done: every arrangement has a register record with contract dates, notice period, cost and the using entities linked, backed by an executed contract.

checklist.step: Populate the provider records with verified identifiers
actions: Record for each provider the legal name, LEI, country of the head office and the country from which the service is actually provided.
Verify each LEI against the GLEIF register and record the registration status - a lapsed LEI must be chased with the provider.
Where a provider genuinely has no LEI, record the alternative identifier permitted by the register format and the reason.
Record the corporate parent so exposure can be aggregated across subsidiaries of the same group.
Set a quarterly refresh on identifier status so lapses are caught before the annual submission.
checklist.done: every provider carries a verified LEI or a justified alternative identifier, a service-provision country and a parent linkage, refreshed quarterly.

checklist.step: Capture the subcontracting chain for critical arrangements
actions: Require every critical provider to disclose in writing the subcontractors supporting the service, with their legal names, LEIs and countries of provision.
Record the chain to the level the register format requires, not just the first tier - the fourth-party cloud region is usually where the real concentration sits.
Check the contract requires prior notification or consent before a material subcontracting change and that the provider has honoured it.
Assess whether any subcontractor sits in a third country and what that means for data access, audit rights and enforceability.
Refresh the disclosure annually and on any provider notification of change.
checklist.done: each critical arrangement carries a written, identifier-level subcontracting chain refreshed annually and on notified change.

checklist.step: Test each critical contract against the required clause set
actions: Map each critical contract against the clause checklist: service description and locations, service levels with measurable targets, incident notification timelines, audit and on-site access rights for the undertaking and the supervisor, sub-outsourcing consent, data protection and data location, continuity and recovery commitments, termination and exit assistance.
Record the clause position per contract - present, absent, or present but weaker than standard - with the clause reference.
Raise a contract amendment for each absent or weak provision on a critical arrangement and track it to signature.
Where a provider refuses an audit or access right, escalate to the Chief Risk Officer for a documented acceptance or a substitution decision.
Feed the clause positions back to the register so the register itself shows contractual completeness.
checklist.done: every critical contract has a clause-by-clause mapping in the register, with amendments raised for every absent or weakened provision.

checklist.step: Review the remuneration and incentive terms in critical arrangements
actions: Read the pricing and incentive mechanics of each critical arrangement - volume bonuses, savings shares, claims-settlement-linked fees, commission ladders for delegated authorities.

Assess whether any mechanism could encourage the provider to take risk the undertaking would not accept for itself - for example a claims handler paid on settlement speed or a delegated underwriter paid on volume without a loss-ratio brake.

Confirm the arrangement is consistent with the undertaking's written remuneration policy under Delegated Regulation Art. 275, including the requirement that it not encourage excessive risk-taking and that it address the integration of sustainability risks as amended by Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/1256.
Record the assessment on the register row and raise a contract change where an incentive is unsound.
Report the outcomes to the Remuneration Committee alongside the internal remuneration policy review.
checklist.done: every critical arrangement carries a recorded incentive-soundness assessment against the remuneration policy, with unsound mechanisms raised as contract changes.

checklist.step: Compute concentration and substitutability positions
actions: Aggregate register spend and function coverage by provider and by corporate parent to find providers supporting multiple critical functions.
Aggregate by underlying infrastructure - cloud provider and region - so several distinct contracts resting on one region are visible as one exposure.
Assess substitutability for each critical provider: is there a viable alternative, how long would migration take, and is the data extractable in a usable format.
Flag any position where a single provider or region failure would breach the RTO of more than one critical function, and take it to the Operational Risk Committee.
Record the concentration conclusion on each affected register row.
checklist.done: concentration is computed by provider, parent and infrastructure region, with substitutability assessed and multi-function exposures escalated.

checklist.step: Maintain a documented exit strategy for every critical arrangement
actions: Write an exit plan per critical arrangement naming the trigger events, the target alternative or in-house route, the migration steps and the estimated duration and cost.
Confirm the contract gives the transition assistance, data return format and continued service period the plan depends on - an exit plan that assumes rights the contract does not grant is not a plan.
Confirm the data return format is machine-readable and tested, ideally by an extract taken during the relationship rather than at its end.
Refresh the plan at each contract renewal and whenever the criticality rating changes.
Record the exit plan reference and its last review date on the register row.
checklist.done: every critical arrangement has a dated exit plan supported by actual contractual rights and a tested data return format.

checklist.step: Notify the supervisory authority of critical outsourcing
actions: Identify any intended outsourcing of a critical or important function and prepare the notification the NCA requires, covering the function, the provider, the rationale, the risk assessment and the oversight arrangements.
Send the notification in good time before the arrangement enters into force so the supervisor can respond - notifying after go-live does not satisfy the obligation.
Notify subsequent material developments in an existing critical outsourcing, including a change of provider, a material change of scope, or the provider's own material subcontracting change.
Record the notification date, the channel and the supervisor's response on the register row and in the regulatory calendar.
checklist.done: every critical outsourcing and material development is notified in advance with the date, channel and supervisory response recorded.

checklist.step: Run monitoring and assurance over live critical providers
actions: Hold the contractual service review at its agreed cadence and record service-level performance against target, not just a satisfaction impression.
Collect and read the provider's assurance evidence - independent audit report, control certification, penetration test summary, continuity test results - and record the exceptions it discloses.
Record every provider incident with its notification timeliness against the contractual window, since late notification is itself a breach.
Escalate persistent service-level failure or refused assurance evidence to the Operational Risk Committee with a substitution recommendation.
Update the provider risk rating on the register from the monitoring outcome.
checklist.done: each critical provider has cadence-held service reviews, read assurance evidence, logged incidents with notification timeliness and an updated risk rating.

checklist.step: Reconcile the register to spend every quarter
actions: Extract all supplier payments for the quarter from the general ledger and accounts payable.
Match each paying supplier to a register arrangement and list every supplier paid with no register entry.
Assess each unmatched supplier for criticality rather than dismissing it on spend size - a small-spend provider can support a critical function.
List register entries with no spend and confirm whether the arrangement has quietly terminated, then close the row with an end date.
Record both break lists and their dispositions on the quarterly reconciliation.
checklist.done: the register reconciles to supplier spend in both directions each quarter with every break assessed and dispositioned.

checklist.step: Submit the annual register of information to the supervisory authority
actions: Generate the register of information in the format and taxonomy the NCA specifies, covering entities, contractual arrangements, providers, functions supported, assessments and subcontracting chains.
Run the format validation and clear every error - unresolved identifier and referential errors are the most common cause of rejection.
Obtain the Chief Risk Officer's approval of the submitted content before upload.
Upload by the date the NCA set, capture the acknowledgement and file it against the reporting year.
Log any rejection and resubmit inside the correction window.
checklist.done: the annual register submission is validated, CRO-approved, uploaded by the NCA's date and evidenced by an acknowledgement.

checklist.step: Report register status to the risk committee and the administrative body
actions: Report quarterly on register completeness, critical arrangements without full contractual rights, concentration positions and open provider incidents.
Present the critical outsourcing decisions taken and pending, with the supervisory notification status of each.
Record the body's decision on each accepted concentration and each contractual gap, with an owner and a date.
Escalate immediately, outside the cycle, any critical function found to be outsourced without a contract or without notification.
checklist.done: the risk committee and administrative body have a quarterly record of register completeness, gaps, concentration and notification status with recorded decisions.

checklist.step: Attest and archive the register
actions: Obtain an annual written attestation from each function owner that the critical arrangements supporting their function are completely and correctly registered.
Snapshot the register at attestation and at each supervisory submission so the position on any date can be reconstructed.
Archive the snapshots with the criticality assessments, clause mappings, subcontracting disclosures, exit plans and notifications.
Apply the 10-year retention label and index by provider, arrangement reference and reporting year.
checklist.done: an annual function-owner attestation and dated register snapshots are archived under a 10-year label and indexed by provider and arrangement.

testing.step: Build the population of third-party arrangements independently of the register
actions: Extract every supplier with spend in the period from procurement and from accounts payable, and every executed agreement from the contract repository.
Merge and de-duplicate the three sources on legal entity name and tax identifier without reference to the register.
Compare the merged population to the register and list every supplier or contract with no register entry.
Sign the population as complete with the extraction date and source system versions.
testing.done: an independently built supplier and contract population is reconciled to the register with every unregistered arrangement listed.

testing.step: Reconcile register entries to executed contracts and to spend
actions: For every register entry, confirm an executed contract exists in the repository with matching parties and dates.
Agree the annual expense recorded on the register to the general ledger spend for that supplier and investigate differences above 10 percent.
List register entries with no contract and contracts with no register entry as exceptions in both directions.
Confirm terminated arrangements carry an end date rather than remaining open indefinitely.
testing.done: every register entry ties to an executed contract and to ledger spend, with breaks in both directions listed.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of arrangements for deep testing
actions: Take 100 percent of arrangements rated critical or important and 100 percent of ICT arrangements supporting a critical function.
Take 15 further arrangements by seeded random selection from the remainder, weighted toward the unregistered population found in step one.
Record the seed, the strata, the population size and the selection date so the sample can be redrawn.
Ensure the sample includes at least one arrangement per entity and per major service category.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all critical and critical-supporting ICT arrangements, and spans every entity and major service category.

testing.step: Re-perform the criticality classification on the sample
actions: For each sampled arrangement, read the service description and independently apply the critical or important function test before looking at the recorded rating.
Cross-check against the continuity critical function inventory - a service underpinning a function on that inventory cannot be rated non-critical.
Compare your conclusion to the recorded rating and treat any downgrade with no documented rationale as an exception.
Confirm a function owner countersigned each rating rather than procurement rating it alone.
testing.done: each sampled criticality rating is independently re-performed against the continuity inventory with a countersignature confirmed.

testing.step: Verify provider identifiers and the subcontracting chain
actions: Run a completeness test across the whole critical population for missing or lapsed LEIs, missing service-provision countries and missing parent linkages.
Verify 20 LEIs directly against the GLEIF register, checking legal name and registration status match the register entry.
For each sampled critical arrangement, request the provider's written subcontracting disclosure and compare it to the recorded chain.
List any critical arrangement whose chain is recorded to first tier only where the register format requires deeper coverage.
testing.done: identifier completeness is tested across the critical population, 20 LEIs are verified at GLEIF, and every sampled subcontracting chain traces to a written disclosure.

testing.step: Test the contractual clause set on sampled critical contracts
actions: Open the executed contract for each sampled critical arrangement and locate each required provision - service levels, incident notification timelines, audit and supervisory access, sub-outsourcing consent, data location and protection, continuity commitments, termination and exit assistance.
Compare the clause actually present to the recorded register position and treat a register entry claiming a provision the contract does not contain as a severe exception.
Check the incident notification window in contract against the notification the undertaking would itself owe its supervisor - a provider window longer than the undertaking's obligation is unworkable.
List every critical contract missing a provision and check whether a CRO acceptance exists.
testing.done: every sampled critical contract is clause-tested against the register position with missing provisions and overstated register entries listed.

testing.step: Re-perform the concentration and exit-strategy assessments
actions: Independently aggregate register arrangements by provider, corporate parent and underlying cloud region and compare to the recorded concentration conclusions.
Identify any provider or region supporting more than one critical function and confirm it was escalated to the Operational Risk Committee.
For each sampled critical arrangement, read the exit plan and confirm every right it relies on exists in the contract.
Confirm the data return format has been tested rather than assumed, and list plans resting on untested extraction.
testing.done: concentration is independently recomputed and every sampled exit plan is confirmed to rest on actual contractual rights and a tested data return.

testing.step: Test supervisory notification and incentive assessment coverage
actions: List every critical outsourcing that entered into force or materially changed in the period and match each to a supervisory notification.
Compare the notification date to the arrangement's effective date and treat notification after go-live as a fail.

For each sampled critical arrangement, confirm the recorded incentive assessment addresses the actual pricing mechanics and references the remuneration policy under Art. 275, including the sustainability-risk integration point added by Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/1256.
List any performance-linked fee structure with no assessment on file.
testing.done: every critical outsourcing traces to a pre-effective-date notification and every sampled incentive structure carries a policy-referenced assessment.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the provider, the arrangement reference, the critical function affected and the gap found.

Assign a root cause from the standard set - arrangement bought outside procurement, criticality downgraded without rationale, LEI never captured, subcontracting not disclosed, clause absent at signature, notification made late, exit plan unsupported.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and escalate any critical function outsourced without a contract or without notification to the CRO the same day.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and, for unnotified critical outsourcing, a same-day CRO escalation.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the register test
actions: Compute register completeness against the independently built population, identifier coverage on critical providers and the clause completeness rate on critical contracts.
State the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - with the workpaper references behind it.
Have the reviewer, who sits outside procurement and vendor management, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and open exceptions to the Risk Committee before the annual register of information is submitted, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper stating completeness, identifier and clause coverage rates with a conclusion is filed and reported before the annual register submission.
